sourceRegistryRecords.officialOwner: City of San Diego Office of the City Treasurer
sourceRegistryRecords.effectiveDateHandling: Version by fiscal year, fee page date, employee-count tier, rental unit tax year, and applicable surcharges.
sourceRegistryRecords.licensingOrUseNotes: Official City Treasurer source; business location and employee count are runtime inputs.
sourceRegistryRecords.runtimeUsePolicy: Use for San Diego business tax certificate and rental unit tax workflows. Do not include in user-facing tax savings totals without confirmed business activity and employee or unit counts.
sourceRegistryRecords.evidenceText: San Diego Treasurer states businesses must obtain a Business Tax Certificate and publishes tax rates and fees, including employee-count based annual amounts.

sourceRegistryRecords.officialOwner: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
sourceRegistryRecords.effectiveDateHandling: Version by tax year and Office of Finance rate table update; separate gross receipts and non-gross classifications.
sourceRegistryRecords.licensingOrUseNotes: Official city source; business activity classification and taxable gross receipts are taxpayer/accountant inputs.
sourceRegistryRecords.runtimeUsePolicy: Use as next-priority Los Angeles local business tax registry source. Keep internal-only until activity classification and tax base are confirmed.
sourceRegistryRecords.evidenceText: Los Angeles Office of Finance publishes current business tax rate tables and non-gross tax rate tables.

sourceRegistryRecords.effectiveDateHandling: Version by BLM service metadata and PLSS update date; treat as legal-description routing support only.
sourceRegistryRecords.licensingOrUseNotes: Official federal cadastral reference; not a county parcel or tax-bill source.
sourceRegistryRecords.runtimeUsePolicy: Use to normalize PLSS-based legal descriptions for assessor search workflows. Customer-facing property tax values require county assessor or treasurer records.
sourceRegistryRecords.evidenceText: BLM provides national PLSS cadastral services representing the PLSS grid and federal land-cadastral reference data.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Import ALDOR state rates and monthly local taxrates.csv snapshots with source retrieval date; local effective dates must be versioned by file month and not backfilled without an archived ALDOR file.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: ALDOR publishes official state sales and use tax rates and a comma-delimited local rates text file for Alabama cities and counties that levy local sales, use, rental, or lodgings taxes. ALDOR also notes local taxes vary and some are not administered by ALDOR, so address-to-local-jurisdiction assignment needs verified city/county treatment.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Treat state general sales/use tax as zero; local Alaska sales tax rates must be resolved from ARSSTC or local municipal sources for the transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Alaska does not levy a state sales tax, but local governments may impose local sales taxes; ARSSTC states Alaska has no state sales tax and more than 100 local taxing jurisdictions, and provides a local sales tax lookup.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Import ADOR monthly CSV tax rate table by business classification; rate changes should respect ADOR notice timing and the transaction period. Address-to-jurisdiction should use ADOR lookup until an official boundary file is verified.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Arizona administers transaction privilege tax rather than a conventional purchaser sales tax; ADOR provides a monthly CSV rate table and an official lookup resource by location and business description that returns state, county, and city rates.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use DFA monthly local tax data and SST quarterly rate and boundary files; version each imported file by official effective quarter or monthly update.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Arkansas DFA provides an official Streamlined Tax Lookup by address or ZIP and downloadable local tax data updated monthly; Arkansas also participates in SST rate and boundary file workflows.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use CDTFA quarterly map/API updates; store tax area code geometry and effective quarter. District taxes must be summed by tax area code for the transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: CDTFA provides an official sales and use tax rate REST API, a map lookup, and ArcGIS feature service data used by the Find Your Tax Rate app; CDTFA states city boundaries, tax rates, and tax area codes are updated quarterly.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use the Colorado DOR GIS API as the primary address-level current source; store response components and retrieval date, and refresh whenever DOR publishes GIS/rate changes.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Colorado DOR provides GIS tools and an API to retrieve state, county, municipal, and special-district sales tax calculation information for a specific address.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Connecticut statewide rate schedule by transaction date; product-specific rates and exemptions must be modeled separately.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Connecticut DRS publishes the state sales and use tax rate and special rates; no local general sales tax boundary is needed for the base statewide rate.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: General sales and use tax rate is zero statewide; gross receipts and other Delaware business taxes are separate non-sales-tax models.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Delaware Division of Revenue states Delaware has no state or local sales tax, while gross receipts tax is imposed separately on businesses.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Version DC rates by statutory effective date; the general rate must reflect scheduled changes, including the Oct. 1, 2026 increase where applicable, and product-specific rates must be separate.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: DC OTR publishes sales and use tax guidance, and the CFO rate table lists general and special rates, including scheduled effective-date changes.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use DOR Address/Jurisdiction Database for point-in-time address jurisdiction and DOR discretionary surtax tables for current and pending rate changes; store effective dates and pending-change status.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Florida DOR provides an Address/Jurisdiction Database for tax rates by address and a discretionary sales surtax rate table; counties may impose local option discretionary surtaxes in addition to state sales tax.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Georgia DOR current, historical, and upcoming rate charts plus SST quarterly rate and boundary files; version by quarter and official effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Georgia DOR publishes sales tax rate charts for current, historical, and upcoming periods, and Georgia appears in SST rate and boundary update files.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Route Hawaii through a GET/use-tax adapter rather than a conventional retail sales-tax model; county surcharge rates must be versioned by county and statutory expiration period.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Hawaii DOTAX publishes General Excise Tax and county surcharge guidance; county surcharge periods and rates differ by county, so county and activity classification are required.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply the statewide Idaho rate by transaction date; local resort-city sales taxes require city ordinance and local tax-base confirmation before inclusion.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Idaho Tax Commission publishes the statewide sales/use tax rate and states some resort cities have voter-approved local sales taxes in addition to state sales tax, with local tax bases that can vary.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Illinois DOR Tax Rate Database and Tax Rate Finder snapshots by tax type and transaction date; preserve fixed-location and location-based distinctions.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Illinois DOR provides an official Tax Rate Database for taxes administered by DOR and a Tax Rate Finder service for location-based rates.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Indiana statewide rate by transaction date; SST detail confirms no local sales/use tax rows are needed for general rate calculation.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Indiana DOR identifies the state sales tax rate, and SST state detail lists no local jurisdiction sales/use taxes for Indiana.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Iowa Tax Mapper and SST files by effective quarter; model Iowa's distinction between local option sales tax and use tax separately.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Iowa provides an official Tax Mapper returning state tax, local option tax, and total tax by address; Iowa guidance states the state rate and explains local option sales tax applicability.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use KDOR quarterly Pub. 1700 files, official address lookup, and SST rate/boundary files; food or other product-specific alternate boundaries must be keyed to product taxability rules.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Kansas DOR publishes quarterly local sales tax updates in Excel and provides an official address lookup; SST notes a Kansas alternate boundary file for food products.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Kentucky statewide rate by transaction date; no local sales/use tax boundary rows are needed for general rate calculation.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Kentucky DOR states sales and use tax is imposed at 6 percent and there are no local sales and use taxes; SST detail is consistent.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Louisiana Uniform Local Sales Tax Board lookup or bulk lookup results by transaction date; store parish, return column, state/local components, and vendor-compensation metadata where returned.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Louisiana provides a Uniform Local Sales Tax Board lookup and bulk lookup tools that return state and local sales tax information by address or geocode.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Maine Revenue Services statewide rate schedule by transaction date; special product or service rates and repealed service-provider-tax treatment require separate taxability rules.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Maine Revenue Services publishes statewide sales and use tax rates and due-date guidance, including the general sales/use rate and special-rate categories.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Maryland statewide sales/use rate by transaction date; product- or service-specific treatment must be modeled separately.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Maryland Comptroller guidance identifies the statewide sales and use tax rate and corresponding use tax treatment for purchases used in Maryland.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Massachusetts statewide sales/use rate by transaction date; local meals, room occupancy, and other non-general taxes are separate models.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Massachusetts DOR guidance publishes the statewide sales and use tax rate; special tax bases must be handled outside the general sales/use rate table.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Michigan statewide sales/use rate by transaction date; no local general sales/use tax boundary table is required.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Michigan Treasury publishes the state sales and use tax rate, and SST detail identifies Michigan as a full member with a statewide rate and no local general sales/use tax.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Minnesota DOR API/rate calculator for current general state and local sales tax rates; store API response date and monitor DOR rate-change publications about 30 days before changes.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Minnesota DOR provides a rate calculator, sales tax rate map, and API that finds general state and local sales tax rates for a Minnesota location.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply statewide Mississippi sales/use rate by transaction date; local tourism and economic-development taxes require separate local tax area and tax-base confirmation.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Mississippi DOR publishes sales tax rates and separate local tourism/economic development tax information, but no comprehensive machine-readable local boundary source was verified.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Missouri DOR enhanced lookup map and annual/period rate tables; version local sales and local use tax components separately by effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Missouri DOR maintains an official sales/use tax rate map intended to provide current rates and boundaries for addresses throughout Missouri, and publishes rate tables by year.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: General state sales/use rate is zero. Montana resort/community local option taxes are not general sales/use taxes and require a separate official local model before inclusion.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Montana does not have a general state sales tax for this model; Montana Revenue publishes local resort tax information, which is a locally approved special tax with its own tax base and should not be imported as a statewide general sales/use rate.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Nebraska DOR quarterly rate and boundary files and rate finder; version by official quarter and transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Nebraska DOR provides local sales/use tax rates, rate and boundary files for download by quarter, and an official sales tax rate finder map.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Nevada official downloadable rate and boundary database files and SST quarterly files; version by official effective quarter.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Nevada Taxation and SST resources identify state and local sales/use rates and official downloadable rate and boundary database files.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: General sales/use tax rate is zero statewide; meals, rooms, communications, and other non-general taxes are separate models.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: New Hampshire DRA states New Hampshire does not have a general sales tax on goods purchased in the state.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply statewide New Jersey rate by transaction date; special zones such as UEZ must be treated as product/location-specific rules, not general local sales tax.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: New Jersey Division of Taxation publishes the statewide sales/use tax rate; SST state detail lists no local general sales/use taxes, and SST provides single-rate New Jersey rate information.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Route New Mexico through a gross-receipts/compensating-tax adapter; use TRD location codes and rate schedules by transaction date, and do not rely on browser-only geocoding as an import source.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: New Mexico TRD provides a Gross Receipts Tax Location Code and Tax Rate Map; TRD explains gross receipts tax rates vary by location because combined rates include state, county, and municipal components.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Import New York rate publications by publication effective date and reporting code; address-to-jurisdiction should remain needs_tax_profile or human review unless an official machine-readable boundary source is added.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: New York Tax Department publishes sales tax rate publications and reporting-code tables, including current and historical local rates; no comprehensive official machine-readable address boundary file was verified in this research pass.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use NCDOR rate and boundary databases together; version each quarterly or dated database file and apply transaction-date effective rules.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: North Carolina DOR publishes a Sales and Use Tax Rate and Boundary Database, explaining that rates and boundaries are used together to determine the correct rate.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use North Dakota rate locator and SST files; version state and local components by effective date and exclude special taxes unless separately modeled.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: North Dakota Tax Department publishes state sales tax guidance and states local city and county taxes may apply; its rate locator includes state and local sales/use tax rates and boundaries.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Ohio Finder address/GPS lookup or registered-user upload database; preserve county and transit authority rate components by transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Ohio's Finder provides official sales/use tax lookup by address, ZIP, or GPS and supports rate and boundary information, including upload databases for registered users.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Oklahoma Tax Commission rate locator, downloadable address database, and SST quarterly files; version by official file effective dates.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Oklahoma provides an official sales/use tax rate locator searchable by address, municipality, county, ZIP, or ZIP+4 and references a downloadable address database; SST detail confirms local rates apply.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: General sales/use tax rate is zero statewide; Oregon vehicle, CAT, lodging, and other taxes are outside this general sales/use rate model.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Oregon DOR states Oregon does not have a general sales, use, or transaction tax, while separate vehicle taxes may apply to specific transactions.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Pennsylvania state rate and local Philadelphia or Allegheny add-ons by transaction location and effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Pennsylvania DOR states the statewide rate is 6 percent, with additional local rates in Allegheny County and Philadelphia; use tax follows the same state and local structure.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Apply Rhode Island statewide rate by transaction date; lodging, hotel, meal, and other special taxes are separate models.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Rhode Island Division of Taxation identifies the sales tax rate as 7 percent and publishes separate guidance for other special taxes.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use SCDOR statewide and local publications plus SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs map for address-level review; do not import customer-facing rates without an official machine-readable boundary or verified lookup result.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: SCDOR publishes a statewide sales/use tax rate and local sales tax guidance, and points users to an official SC District Information search map for address rate questions; no comprehensive import-ready boundary file was verified.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use South Dakota DOR/SST rate and boundary database files by effective quarter; version local and state components separately.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: South Dakota DOR sales/use tax resources reference rate and boundary database files, and SST provides updated South Dakota rate and boundary files.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Tennessee DOR downloadable rate tables and boundary database, TNMap address lookup, and SST quarterly files by effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Tennessee DOR says taxpayers may download local sales tax rate tables and a boundary database, and TNMap provides a Streamlined Sales Tax jurisdictional and rate database by address.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Comptroller address locator, local jurisdiction tax rate file, and quarterly updates; cap combined local sales/use rate according to official Texas rules and version by effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Texas Comptroller provides an official Sales Tax Rate Locator, local tax rate tables, and a downloadable address dataset with associated state and local responsibilities and local jurisdiction rate files.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Utah Tax Commission SST rate and boundary files and TAP address lookup; version by SST effective quarter and transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Utah Tax Commission directs users to SST boundary files for sourcing and provides TAP address lookup by street address or full ZIP+4 for rate and jurisdiction.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use SST Vermont rate and boundary files by effective quarter; local option sales taxes must be tied to municipality and effective date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: SST state detail identifies Vermont as a state with local jurisdiction sales/use taxes, and SST publishes Vermont rate and boundary files including 2026 updates.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Virginia Tax locality code/rate lookup and downloadable Excel rates; rate depends on the locality where the sale or receipt occurs, with regional and product-specific rules separate.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Virginia Tax provides a sales tax rate and locality code lookup map and downloadable rate data; Virginia guidance states rates vary by locality or where merchandise is received.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Washington DOR lookup, address files, and jurisdiction shapefiles; version local location codes and rates by effective date and transaction destination.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Washington DOR provides official sales/use tax lookup by address, ZIP+4, or map, downloadable address files, and shapefiles for sales tax jurisdiction boundaries.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use West Virginia Tax Division municipal sales/use tax rate and boundary tables and SST files; version municipal adoption and effective dates separately from state rate.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: West Virginia Tax Division publishes municipal sales/use tax information, including comma-delimited data files with a boundary table and tax rate table, and participates in SST rate and boundary files.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Wisconsin DOR lookup and downloadable rate and boundary database files; version county/city/stadium or special components by transaction date.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Wisconsin DOR provides a state and local sales tax rate lookup and downloadable rate and boundary database files; lookup supports street address and nine-digit ZIP.

taxRateImportPlans.effectiveDateHandling: Use Wyoming DOR rate charts and SST rate/boundary files by effective quarter; county option and lodging components must be separated from general sales/use where applicable.
taxRateImportPlans.evidenceText: Wyoming DOR publishes sales/use/lodging tax rates, and SST state detail/rate-boundary files provide state and local rate/boundary support.

eligibleItems: qualified solar energy devices sold or leased by a registered Arizona solar energy device retailer or lessor
solar equipment eligible for Arizona TPT deduction code treatment
excludedItems: non-solar equipment
transactions by sellers not registered as solar energy device retailers or lessors where registration is required
contracting charges not qualifying under Arizona's MRRA or solar device deduction rules
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Arizona DOR states that a solar energy device installed on a qualifying MRRA project is not subject to tax and identifies deduction code 500. Arizona DOR ruling/form sources describe the deduction for sales or leases of qualified solar energy devices and require retailer/lessor registration and exemption/deduction documentation.

eligibleItems: tangible personal property purchased by a CAEATFA participating party for an approved project
tangible personal property purchased by a construction contractor for use in a construction contract for a CAEATFA participating party
approved projects involving alternative energy sources
approved projects involving advanced transportation technologies
approved nuclear fusion electrical generation facilities after SB 86 expansion
excludedItems: projects not approved by CAEATFA
property functionally used or placed in service before approval when approval conditions are not met
ordinary retrofit work without CAEATFA participation
labor charges except to the extent embedded in taxable-measure rules for qualifying property under contractor guidance
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: CDTFA states RTC section 6010.8 provides a sales and use tax exclusion for tangible personal property purchased by a participating party or contractor for eligible CAEATFA projects involving alternative energy sources, advanced transportation technologies, advanced manufacturing, and recycled feedstock. CDTFA states the taxpayer must apply to CAEATFA and use an exclusion certificate; SB 86 extended the sunset to January 1, 2028.

eligibleItems: construction contracts involving fixtures such as air conditioning units, furnaces, prefabricated cabinets, and signs
construction contracts involving machinery and equipment
excludedItems: transactions covered by a separate statutory exemption or exclusion such as CAEATFA
out-of-state use certificates and federal government contract exceptions unless separately supported
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 0.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: CDTFA states California treats construction contractors as consumers of materials and retailers of fixtures they install. Tax applies to the contractor's cost of materials, to the selling price of fixtures, and to the gross receipts from machinery and equipment furnished and installed. CDTFA also states many labor charges are taxable, fabrication labor is taxable, and special rules apply to houses, buildings, and real property.

eligibleItems: components used in the production of alternating current electricity from a renewable energy source
solar photovoltaic components that produce AC electricity
wind, geothermal, biomass, and other qualifying renewable electricity production components
excludedItems: non-qualifying monitoring or equipment not used in renewable AC electricity production
most state-administered city and county sales taxes unless local treatment is separately verified
home energy efficiency equipment not used to produce AC electricity
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Colorado DOR guidance states Colorado allows a sales and use tax exemption for components used in the production of alternating current electricity from a renewable energy source. DOR states the exemption generally applies to state-administered special district sales taxes but not to most state-administered city and county sales taxes.

eligibleItems: equipment related to qualifying solar or geothermal systems
services relating to installation of qualifying systems
ice storage cooling systems where covered by CERT-140 guidance
excludedItems: non-qualifying conventional HVAC equipment
repairs or unrelated real property services not relating to installation of qualifying systems
equipment not documented on the required Connecticut exemption certificate
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Connecticut DRS states legislation exempts sales of solar energy electricity generating systems, passive or active solar water or space heating systems, geothermal resource systems, related equipment, and services relating to installation of the systems. DRS exemption pages identify CERT-140 as the certificate for solar, geothermal, and ice storage cooling system claims.

eligibleItems: machinery used directly in renewable energy technology industries
equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and fuel used directly in renewable energy technology industries
machinery, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and fuel used directly in clean energy technology industries
excludedItems: ordinary building retrofit equipment outside a qualifying renewable or clean energy technology industry
installation labor unless independently exempt
general administrative, office, or facility equipment not directly used in the qualifying industry
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Connecticut CERT-142 certifies purchases of machinery, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and fuel used directly in renewable energy and clean energy technology industries under Conn. Gen. Stat. section 12-412(117)(B).

eligibleItems: equipment and requisite hardware used for collecting solar energy
equipment and requisite hardware used for transferring solar energy
equipment and requisite hardware used for converting solar energy
equipment and requisite hardware used for storing solar energy
equipment and requisite hardware used for using incident solar energy
excludedItems: non-solar building equipment
installation labor unless separately exempt or nontaxable under Florida construction-contracting rules
components not within the Florida solar energy system definition
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Florida DOR states Florida law exempts solar energy systems and all components of such systems from sales and use tax. DOR defines solar energy system as equipment and requisite hardware that collect, transfer, convert, store, or use incident solar energy. Florida construction-contracting guidance must still be applied to installation and real property improvement charges.

eligibleItems: solar equipment directly related to a qualifying system
wind-powered system equipment directly related to a qualifying system
heat-pump system equipment directly related to a qualifying system
equipment used as a primary or auxiliary power system for heating or supplying energy needs of a taxpayer's principal residence in Massachusetts
excludedItems: systems not used for the taxpayer's principal residence in Massachusetts
second homes
commercial property under the principal-residence exemption
installation labor unless separately nontaxable or exempt
equipment not directly related to the qualifying solar, wind, or heat pump system
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Massachusetts DOR and the state tax expenditure budget state equipment directly related to solar, wind-powered, or heat-pump systems is exempt from sales and use tax when the system is used as a primary or auxiliary power system for heating or supplying the energy needs of the taxpayer's principal residence in Massachusetts.

eligibleItems: photovoltaic solar energy system machinery used directly and exclusively in furnishing electricity
energy storage system equipment used at a photovoltaic electricity generation facility where qualified under Massachusetts machinery exemption analysis
software incorporated into or functioning as an adjunct to exempt machinery when supported by ruling facts
excludedItems: equipment not used directly and exclusively in furnishing electricity
facts outside the specific Massachusetts letter ruling framework
ordinary residential batteries not independently supported by principal residence or machinery exemption facts
installation labor unless independently exempt
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Massachusetts letter rulings have treated PV systems and certain energy storage equipment as exempt machinery when used directly and exclusively in furnishing electricity. Because letter rulings are fact-specific, runtime modeling must confirm the facility, equipment, and direct/exclusive use facts before customer-facing savings are shown.

excludedItems: commercial wind equipment not within the residential wind equipment exemption
non-energy building equipment
installation labor unless independently nontaxable or exempt
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maryland Comptroller sales and use tax publication states sales and use tax does not apply to sales of geothermal equipment, residential wind energy equipment, and solar energy equipment. Contractor guidance should be used to classify real property installation charges.

eligibleItems: machinery and equipment used directly and predominantly in production activities
machinery and equipment used to generate electricity for sale
machinery and equipment used to generate electricity for use in a production activity
excludedItems: electric generation not for sale or not for use in production activity
general building equipment
distribution or administrative equipment not used directly and predominantly in production
installation labor unless independently exempt
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maryland Comptroller states sales and use tax does not apply to sales of machinery and equipment used directly and predominantly in production activities, including generating electricity for sale or for use in a production activity.

eligibleItems: electricity sold at an electric vehicle charging station
electricity used to charge an electric vehicle and not sold under a residential or domestic rate schedule
excludedItems: electricity sold under a residential or domestic rate schedule
charging equipment purchase taxability, which must be analyzed separately
installation of charging equipment, which must be analyzed separately
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 0.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maryland Comptroller instructions for SUT202 require reporting sales of electricity for charging electric vehicles subject to the 6% rate, including sales at EV charging stations and electricity used to charge EVs that is not sold under a residential or domestic rate schedule. Sales/use tax savings should be zero unless an exemption applies.

eligibleItems: solar energy systems under Minnesota Statutes section 297A.67 subdivision 29
excludedItems: non-solar building equipment
installation labor unless independently exempt or nontaxable
equipment not qualifying as a solar energy system
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Minnesota Revenue's industry guide lists Solar energy systems under Minnesota Statutes section 297A.67, subdivision 29. Minnesota Revenue states sellers do not collect sales tax on nontaxable sales when the purchaser gives a completed Form ST3 Certificate of Exemption.

eligibleItems: materials used to manufacture wind energy conversion systems
materials used to install wind energy conversion systems
materials used to construct wind energy conversion systems
materials used to repair wind energy conversion systems
materials used to replace wind energy conversion systems
excludedItems: non-wind equipment
general building materials not used for the wind energy conversion system
installation labor unless independently exempt
operations or maintenance services not included in the material exemption
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Minnesota Revenue's industry guide lists Wind energy conversion systems and materials used to manufacture, install, construct, repair, or replace them under Minnesota Statutes section 297A.68, subdivision 12. Form ST3 is the state exemption certificate used to document exempt purchases.

eligibleItems: solar panels that are part of a solar photovoltaic energy system
tracking systems and SCADA system control center when qualifying under Missouri DOR ruling facts
components necessary to construct a solar photovoltaic energy system purchased by a company for sale or lease to an end user
components for a utility-scale system used to produce, collect, and transmit electricity for resale or retail sale
excludedItems: homeowner self-purchases where the system is not purchased by a company and sold to an end user
materials not part of the solar photovoltaic energy system
installation labor unless independently exempt
transactions not within section 144.030.2(46), RSMo, and section 144.615.3, RSMo
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Missouri DOR letter ruling states purchases of listed solar PV system components are exempt under section 144.030.2(46), RSMo, and section 144.615.3, RSMo. Missouri DOR FAQ states the solar panel system exemption applies if purchased or constructed and sold or leased to an end user or used to produce, collect, and transmit electricity for resale or retail sale, and that homeowner self-purchases are not eligible.

eligibleItems: qualified property for use in the manufacture of qualified C-BED projects
qualified property for use in the installation of qualified C-BED projects
qualified property for use in the construction of qualified C-BED projects
qualified property for use in the repair or replacement of qualified C-BED projects
qualified community-based energy development wind, solar, biomass, and landfill gas projects where approved
excludedItems: projects without Nebraska Department of Revenue C-BED application approval
property outside the qualified C-BED project
ordinary residential or commercial solar installations not qualifying as C-BED projects
contractor labor unless independently treated as nontaxable contractor labor
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Sales/use tax exemption percent: 1.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Nebraska DOR lists C-BED purchases as materials for manufacture, installation, construction, repair, or replacement of a community-based energy development project. DOR's C-BED guide states purchases of qualified property for use in qualified C-BED projects are exempt from Nebraska and local sales taxes and the project developer must file a C-BED application; approved developers receive a sales and use tax certificate of exemption.

eligibleItems: solar systems designed to provide heating
solar systems designed to provide cooling
solar systems designed to provide electrical power
solar systems designed to provide mechanical power
solar energy storage devices when qualifying as part of the solar system
excludedItems: non-solar building equipment
installation labor unless treated as exempt capital improvement labor
repairs or maintenance not qualifying as exempt capital improvement

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Solar water heating credit equals 35% of actual cost subject to caps of $2,250 for single-family residential property, $350 per unit for multi-family residential property, and $250,000 for commercial property. Other solar credit equals 35% of actual cost subject to caps of $5,000 for single-family residential property, $350 per unit for multi-family residential property, and $500,000 for commercial property. Wind credit equals 20% of actual cost subject to caps of $1,500 for single-family residential property, $200 per unit for multi-family residential property, and $500,000 for commercial property. Solar excess credit may be elected refundable with a 30% reduction; certain low-income or retirement-income taxpayers may elect full refundability. Otherwise unused credit carries forward until exhausted.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: case when technology='solar_water_heating' then min(0.35 * actual_cost_cents, applicable_hi_swh_cap_cents) when technology='other_solar' then min(0.35 * actual_cost_cents, applicable_hi_other_solar_cap_cents) when technology='wind' then min(0.20 * actual_cost_cents, applicable_hi_wind_cap_cents) end

taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Unused nonrefundable credit may be carried forward until exhausted.

other renewable energy source devices listed in Florida statute
eligibleApplicantTypes: owner of residential real property with qualifying renewable energy source device
owner of nonresidential real property with qualifying renewable energy source device
tangible personal property taxpayer with qualifying renewable energy source device
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying residential real property, the just value attributable to the renewable energy source device is not considered in assessment. For qualifying nonresidential real property, 80% of the just value attributable to the device is excluded. For qualifying tangible personal property, 80% of assessed value is exempt.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: case when property_class='residential_real_property' then attributable_just_value_cents when property_class='nonresidential_real_property' then 0.80 * attributable_just_value_cents when property_class='tangible_personal_property' then 0.80 * assessed_value_cents end
requiredDocuments: tangible personal property return if applicable
records supporting assessor value attributable to the device
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Florida Statutes §193.624 excludes the residential just value attributable to renewable energy source devices and excludes 80% of attributable just value for nonresidential real property, with device categories listed in statute. Florida Statutes §196.182 provides an 80% tangible personal property exemption for qualifying renewable energy source devices; Florida DOR tangible personal property return materials identify the renewable energy source device exemption. ([Online Sunshine][17])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption or assessment exclusion.

eligibleApplicantTypes: California real property owner adding a qualifying active solar energy system
developer or initial purchaser subject to special BOE rules
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying active solar energy system construction or addition is excluded from new construction for California property tax assessment; therefore the system value is not added to assessed value solely because of the solar addition, subject to statutory sunset and BOE rules.
requiredDocuments: BOE or county assessor form if required for developer or initial purchaser transaction
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: California BOE states the active solar energy system exclusion was extended through the 2025-26 fiscal year and is scheduled to sunset January 1, 2027. BOE FAQ materials state qualifying active solar energy systems may be excluded from new construction under Revenue and Taxation Code §73, and BOE forms guidance states no filing is generally required when a property owner adds active solar to an existing structure and the assessor receives the building permit. ([California State Board of Equalization][18])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax new-construction exclusion.

eligibleApplicantTypes: Maine property owner with qualifying solar energy equipment
taxpayer filing exemption application with local assessor by April 1
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying solar energy equipment is exempt from property tax if it satisfies the current statutory use or net-energy-billing requirements and the taxpayer files with the local assessor by April 1 for the first year the exemption is requested.
requiredDocuments: Maine renewable energy or solar energy equipment exemption application
utility bill credit or on-site use documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maine Revenue Services property tax materials describe a renewable energy investment exemption and require application by April 1 in the first year requested. Current MRS Bulletin 29 states that, for assessments on or after April 1, 2025, certain solar equipment that generates heat or electricity is exempt; Maine statutes provide real and personal property provisions for solar energy equipment. ([Maine][19])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption.

eligibleItems: certified renewable energy system producing on-site energy for a building
eligibleApplicantTypes: New Jersey property owner with certified renewable energy system
taxpayer filing Form CRES with local tax assessor
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Exemption amount equals the difference between assessed value with the certified renewable energy system and assessed value without the system; exemption is effective for the tax year following certification and thereafter while the system is used primarily for the qualifying purpose.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: New Jersey Treasury states the renewable energy system property tax exemption equals the difference between total assessed value before and after the system is installed and requires Form CRES with the tax assessor. Form CRES states the exemption is effective for the tax year following the year certification is granted and thereafter during qualifying use. ([NJ.gov][20])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption.

eligibleApplicantTypes: Wisconsin property owner with qualifying renewable energy system
taxpayer submitting PR-303 documentation to local assessor
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying biogas, synthetic gas, solar, and wind energy systems are exempt from Wisconsin general property tax, excluding conventional building or equipment components that do not qualify.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Wisconsin DOR guidance states biogas, synthetic gas, solar, and wind energy systems are exempt from general property tax and distinguishes qualifying systems from conventional components. Form PR-303 instructs taxpayers to submit exemption documentation to the local assessor by March 1 and lists supporting documentation such as specifications, manufacturer information, capacity, and operating requirements. ([Wisconsin Department of Revenue][21])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption.

eligibleItems: solar energy generating system personal property
eligibleApplicantTypes: Minnesota property owner with qualifying solar energy generating system personal property
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Personal property consisting of a solar energy generating system is exempt from property tax. Real property used primarily for solar energy production may be subject to separate classification and production tax rules, including a solar energy production tax for systems over 1 MW AC.
requiredDocuments: Minnesota production tax filing or exemption documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Minnesota Statutes §272.02, subd. 24 exempts personal property consisting of solar energy generating systems. Minnesota Revenue states the solar energy production tax is $1.20 per MWh for systems over 1 MW AC, while systems of 1 MW AC or less are exempt from the production tax. ([MN Revisor's Office][22])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption.

eligibleItems: alternative energy system qualifying under Montana law and regulation
eligibleApplicantTypes: Montana residential property owner
Montana nonresidential property owner
taxpayer applying with local Montana Department of Revenue field office by March 1
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Installation cost or market value attributable to a qualifying alternative energy system may be exempt from property tax for 10 years, subject to statutory and regulatory caps and local Department of Revenue approval.
requiredDocuments: Montana Form AB-14 or current alternative energy system exemption application
local Department of Revenue field office confirmation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Montana Department of Revenue Form AB-14 states the installation cost of an alternative energy system in residential or nonresidential property may be eligible for a 10-year property tax exemption if it meets §15-6-224 and ARM 42.19.1104, with filing to the local DOR field office by March 1. Regulation text identifies residential and nonresidential exemption caps, but assessor confirmation is required before modeling savings. ([Montana Department of Revenue][23])
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption.

eligibleItems: approved renewable energy operations in a Michigan Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone
eligibleApplicantTypes: company or project specifically approved for Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone benefits
taxpayer with qualifying operations within approved zone boundaries
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Potential exemption is project-specific and may apply to actual eligible state education tax, real property tax, personal property tax, and local income tax lines for approved operations within an approved zone, subject to local approvals, zone term, phaseout multiplier, compliance, and official abatement documentation.
requiredDocuments: approved Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone designation
approved zone legal description and maps
property tax bills or assessor records
state and local tax compliance documentation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: RetroFi's supplied source-backed runtime rule states Michigan Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone benefits are approved-zone and company/project-specific, apply only to designated operations within approved geographic boundaries, and require approved program documents, local approvals, compliance, and assessor or tax documentation.
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable to property tax exemption; any income tax treatment must be separately confirmed from return instructions and approved program documents.

eligibleItems: processing for hire for solar energy systems or components
manufacturer wholesale sales of qualifying solar products
eligibleApplicantTypes: Washington taxpayer with qualifying solar manufacturing, processing for hire, or manufacturer-wholesale activity
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: This is a Washington B&O tax rate preference, not a state income/franchise credit, depreciation deduction, or property tax exemption. Route to gross_receipts_or_bo_rate_preference model, not this state tax credit/exemption/deduction schema.
requiredDocuments: annual tax performance report filing confirmation
Multiple Activities Tax Credit documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: RetroFi's supplied runtime rule classifies the Washington solar manufacturing benefit as a state B&O rate-preference workflow under RCW 82.04.294, with locality not affecting the state rate and with tax-return classification, deductions, MATC, and annual tax performance report inputs required. The requested schema does not include B&O or gross receipts rate-preference modelKind, so this is unsupported here.
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable.

eligibleItems: renewable energy resources and associated equipment subject to Rhode Island statutory tax valuation
eligibleApplicantTypes: Rhode Island property owner with renewable energy resource or associated equipment
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Rhode Island's rule is a property tax special valuation or assessor workflow, not a simple credit, deduction, or exemption in this schema. It requires AC capacity, resource type, municipal assessor jurisdiction, commercial or residential classification, municipal waiver or exemption status, tangible and real property treatment, interconnection status, and counterfactual ordinary tax before any savings value is modeled.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: RetroFi's supplied runtime rule states Rhode Island has statewide statutory per-kW treatment for renewable energy resources and associated equipment but municipal assessor jurisdiction still matters for administration, local ordinance waivers, tax-bill treatment, and counterfactual property-tax savings. The requested schema lacks property_tax_special_valuation, so this is unsupported here.
taxRuleRecords.carryforward: Not applicable.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying onsite solar and listed energy improvements, the statutory added property value is zero when the statutory documentation conditions are satisfied.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Arizona law states that specified solar energy devices and other qualified energy equipment are considered to add no value to the property, and separately requires documentation of acquisition and installation costs for energy efficient building components, renewable energy equipment, and combined heat and power systems.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Documentation generally must be provided not later than six months before notice of full cash value; if added after September 30, documentation is due by March 31 of the initial valuation year.

eligibleItems: transmission equipment used for renewable generation
distribution equipment used for renewable generation
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Through the statutory period, taxable renewable energy and storage equipment subject to this section is valued at 20% of depreciated cost.
requiredDocuments: renewable energy equipment report if required
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: A.R.S. 42-14155 provides that, through December 31, 2040, the full cash value of taxable renewable energy and storage equipment is 20% of depreciated cost. Arizona Department of Revenue publishes a renewable energy equipment property tax form.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying active solar energy system construction is excluded from new construction, so the qualifying solar added value does not increase assessed value while the statutory exclusion applies.
requiredDocuments: claim documentation if required by assessor
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: California describes the incentive as a new construction exclusion, not an exemption. Revenue and Taxation Code section 73 excludes qualifying active solar energy systems from newly constructed property through the 2025-26 fiscal year, with a scheduled January 1, 2027 sunset.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Initial purchaser claim may be required within three years for qualifying owner-builder initial construction situations.

eligibleItems: passive solar water or space heating
active solar water or space heating
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying renewable energy systems are exempt from property tax. For certain commercial or industrial solar thermal or geothermal systems, the exemption is limited to assessed value exceeding the conventional system portion.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: exempt_assessed_value_cents = qualified_system_assessed_value_cents; for commercial_industrial_solar_thermal_or_geothermal: exempt_assessed_value_cents = max(0, system_assessed_value_cents - conventional_system_assessed_value_cents)
requiredDocuments: load or beneficial account documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Connecticut General Statutes chapter 203 includes property tax exemptions for qualifying residential, farm, commercial, and industrial Class I renewable, hydropower, solar thermal, and geothermal systems, and requires a written application by November 1.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: November 1 application deadline with the assessor or board of assessors.

eligibleItems: solar photovoltaic systems over 1 MW AC
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Certain solar photovoltaic systems over 1 MW AC are subject to a uniform solar capacity tax of $10,000 per MW of nameplate capacity for the statutory period, subject to exclusions and later legislative changes requiring refresh review.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Connecticut legislative summaries for 2025 describe a uniform $10,000 per MW solar capacity tax for certain photovoltaic systems over 1 MW AC with permission to operate on or after July 1, 2026. Because 2026 legislation may revise implementation details, runtime use should require current-law review.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Residential real property value attributable to a renewable energy source device is excluded at 100%. Nonresidential real property value attributable to the device is excluded at 80%. Renewable energy source device tangible personal property is exempt at 80%.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if residential_real_property: exempt_value_cents = device_value_cents; if nonresidential_real_property_or_tpp: exempt_value_cents = round(0.80 * device_value_cents)
requiredDocuments: tangible personal property record if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Florida Statutes section 193.624 excludes renewable energy source device value from real property just value at 100% for residential property and 80% for nonresidential property. Section 196.182 exempts 80% of assessed value of renewable energy source device tangible personal property and sunsets the nonresidential provisions after December 31, 2037.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: The statutory gross earnings tax is imposed in lieu of property tax on exempt renewable energy producer property. Wind and geothermal are taxed at 3% of gross earnings; solar is taxed at 3.5% of gross earnings.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if technology in ['wind','geothermal']: annual_tax_cents = round(gross_earnings_cents * 0.03); if technology == 'solar': annual_tax_cents = round(gross_earnings_cents * 0.035)
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Idaho Code section 63-3502B imposes a gross earnings tax on wind, solar, and geothermal producers in lieu of the property taxes on property exempted under the renewable producer property exemption. Administrative rules address distribution of the gross earnings tax.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: A qualifying owner may claim alternate valuation. The chief county assessment officer values the improvements as if equipped with conventional equipment and as equipped with solar; the lower valuation applies while the system is used.
requiredDocuments: claim filed with chief county assessment officer
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: 35 ILCS 200/10-10 allows a solar energy system owner to claim alternate valuation by filing with the chief county assessment officer, who compares conventional-equipment value with solar-equipped value and applies the lower value.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For covered commercial solar energy systems in counties with population under 3,000,000, fair cash value is the trended real property cost basis less physical depreciation, with a statutory minimum of 30% of trended cost basis. The Department of Revenue publishes annual trend factors.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: trended_cost_cents = 21800000 * nameplate_mw * assessment_year_trending_factor; depreciated_value_cents = trended_cost_cents - min((actual_age_years / 25) * trended_cost_cents, 0.70 * trended_cost_cents); fair_cash_value_cents = max(depreciated_value_cents, 0.30 * trended_cost_cents)
requiredDocuments: survey or legal description for ground-installed systems
Department of Revenue annual valuation publication
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Illinois law establishes a commercial solar valuation method for counties under 3,000,000 population. The Department of Revenue 2026 publication uses a $218,000 per MW real property cost basis, a 2026 trend factor of 1.31, and depreciation over 25 years with a 30% floor.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying utility-grade solar facilities, the land portion of the fixed property is assessed at an amount not exceeding the Department of Local Government Finance solar land base rate for the region.
requiredDocuments: DLGF annual solar land base rate publication
facility layout showing land underneath, between, and immediately surrounding panels
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Indiana DLGF guidance states that, after December 31, 2021, the land portion of fixed property of a utility-grade solar energy installation facility is assessed at an amount not exceeding the solar land base rate for the region.

eligibleItems: solar or wind storage and point-of-use equipment
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Construction or installation of a solar energy system, including the statutory wind-energy definition, does not increase actual, assessed, or taxable value for five full assessment years.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: taxable_added_value_cents = 0 for assessment_years 1 through 5 after construction_or_installation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Iowa Code section 441.21 provides that construction or installation of solar energy systems on agricultural, residential, commercial, or industrial property shall not increase actual, assessed, or taxable values for five full assessment years. The definition includes conversion of incident solar radiation or wind energy and storage or point-of-use equipment.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: The value added by new or refitted geothermal heating or cooling construction or installation on residential property is exempt for ten years.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Iowa Revenue and Iowa Code section 427.1 describe a ten-year property tax exemption for residential geothermal heating and cooling systems installed on or after July 1, 2012, with a February 1 first-year filing deadline.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: February 1 of the first assessment year for which the exemption is requested.

eligibleItems: battery energy storage when qualifying as part of renewable generation property
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Property actually and regularly used predominantly to produce and generate electricity from renewable energy resources may be exempt. For exemptions after December 31, 2016, the exemption period is ten taxable years immediately following completion of construction or installation.
requiredDocuments: Board of Tax Appeals exemption application and order
battery energy storage documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Kansas Department of Revenue lists a renewable energy property exemption under K.S.A. 79-201 Eleventh and states that post-2016 exemptions run for ten taxable years. KDOR guidance states renewable exemptions must be applied for and granted by BOTA, with annual renewal if granted.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Apply upon project completion and/or initial production; annual renewal is required if the exemption is granted.

eligibleSectors: community solar or net billing facilities subject to statutory conditions
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualified solar energy equipment is exempt from property tax when the statutory onsite-use or net-billing subscription conditions are met.
requiredDocuments: net billing or onsite-use documentation if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maine statutes exempt qualifying solar energy equipment as personal property and real estate. Maine Revenue describes the Renewable Energy Investment Exemption as beginning April 1, 2020 and requiring taxpayers to apply by April 1 of the first year requested.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: April 1 of the first property tax year for which the exemption is requested.

eligibleSectors: commercial for solar energy property where statutory definition is met
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Solar energy property and residential wind energy equipment are not subject to real property tax.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Maryland Tax-Property section 7-242 defines solar energy property and provides that residential wind energy equipment and solar energy property are not subject to real property tax.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualified solar or wind systems, including qualifying co-located storage, are exempt for twenty years if they meet one of the statutory size, load, or PILOT paths. PILOT agreements may substitute for ordinary property tax treatment when applicable.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if exemption_path_confirmed: exempt_value_cents = qualified_system_assessed_value_cents for up to 20 years; if pilot_path_confirmed: payment_cents = approved_pilot_agreement_payment_cents
requiredDocuments: DOER incentive or permission to operate verification if applicable
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Massachusetts General Laws chapter 59, section 5, clause Forty-fifth exempts owned or leased solar and wind powered systems, including qualifying co-located storage, for twenty years when statutory production, size, or PILOT conditions are met.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: A qualifying fuel cell system installed after January 1, 2020 that is capable of producing not more than 125% of the annual energy needs of the property is exempt under the statutory clause.
requiredDocuments: energy output and property energy need documentation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Massachusetts clause Forty-fifth B exempts qualifying fuel cell systems installed after January 1, 2020 when the system is capable of producing not more than 125% of the annual energy needs of the property.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying residential alternative energy systems with capacity not exceeding 150 kW and annual output not exceeding annual consumption are not considered an increase in true cash value until the property is sold.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Michigan State Tax Commission Bulletin 6 of 2020 explains that alternative energy systems on residential real property are excluded from assessment true cash value until sold if the system is not over 150 kW and annual output does not exceed annual consumption.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying alternative energy personal property used solely to offset commercial or industrial energy usage on the host property may be exempt if capacity and value limits are satisfied.
requiredDocuments: personal property statement or assessor record
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Michigan State Tax Commission Bulletin 6 of 2020 states that alternative energy personal property for commercial or industrial property is exempt if statutory requirements are met, including a 150 kW capacity limit and use solely to offset host-property energy usage.

eligibleItems: onsite battery storage included in approved application
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: An approved solar energy facility exemption certificate exempts the facility from ad valorem real and personal property taxes for 20 years and substitutes the Solar Energy Facilities Tax. The general rate is $7,000 per MW AC, with a reduced $2,000 per MW AC rate for qualifying reduced-rate sites and a construction-in-progress reduction during construction.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: annual_specific_tax_cents = nameplate_mw_ac * (200000 if reduced_rate_site_qualifies else 700000); if construction_in_progress_percent < 100: annual_specific_tax_cents = annual_specific_tax_cents * 0.50
requiredDocuments: approved solar energy facility exemption certificate
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Michigan Treasury explains that a solar energy facility exemption certificate provides a 20-year exemption from ad valorem property taxes and imposes a Solar Energy Facilities Tax. MCL 211.1159 provides the $7,000 per MW AC general rate and reduced $2,000 per MW AC rate for qualifying facilities. No new exemption is available after December 31, 2031.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Application must be filed before the facility is placed in service; State Tax Commission applications received on or after September 30 may be processed the following year.

eligibleItems: renewable energy operations approved for a Renaissance Zone
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone treatment is project-specific. If an approved zone, approved company operations, parcel boundary, tax compliance, local approvals, and phaseout schedule are confirmed, eligible approved tax lines may be abated under the approved zone documents.
requiredDocuments: approved zone maps and legal description
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Michigan Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone benefits are approved-zone and company/project-specific. The current RetroFi package correctly treats this as a workflow requiring approved zone documents, legal boundaries, local approvals, compliance, and actual abated tax lines before showing savings.

eligibleItems: solar energy generating systems over 1 MW AC
solar energy generating systems 1 MW AC or less
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Solar energy generating system personal property is exempt from property tax. Systems over 1 MW AC pay a solar energy production tax of $1.20 per MWh; systems 1 MW AC or less are exempt from the production tax. Land remains subject to applicable classification and property tax.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if nameplate_mw_ac > 1: annual_production_tax_cents = mwh_produced * 120; else: annual_production_tax_cents = 0
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Minnesota exempts personal property consisting of solar energy generating systems and imposes a $1.20 per MWh solar energy production tax on systems over 1 MW AC. The owner must file the annual report by January 15; late reporting may trigger the statutory nameplate-capacity calculation.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: January 15 annual production report; extension up to 15 days may be available.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Wind energy conversion system real and personal property is exempt except land. Wind production tax applies by system size using statutory cents-per-kWh rates.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if nameplate_mw <= 0.25 or qualifying_political_subdivision_system_exempt: annual_production_tax_cents = 0; else if nameplate_mw > 12: annual_production_tax_cents = mwh_produced * 120; else if nameplate_mw > 2: annual_production_tax_cents = mwh_produced * 36; else: annual_production_tax_cents = mwh_produced * 12
requiredDocuments: Department of Revenue wind production report
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Minnesota exempts wind energy conversion system real and personal property except land and imposes wind energy production tax by size. The statutory rates are 0.12 cents/kWh for large systems, 0.036 cents/kWh for medium systems, and 0.012 cents/kWh for small systems, with annual reporting due January 15.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: A portion of the appraised value of capital investment in recognized nonfossil energy generation or low-emission wood or biomass devices is exempt for ten years, capped at $20,000 for single-family residential property and $100,000 for multifamily residential or nonresidential property.
requiredDocuments: local Department of Revenue field office confirmation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Montana Code Annotated section 15-6-224 exempts specified appraised value of capital investments in recognized nonfossil energy generation or low-emission wood or biomass devices for ten years. Montana Revenue Form AB-14 states the application is due to the local DOR field office by March 1.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: March 1 for the current tax year.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Machinery and equipment in a qualifying electrical generation facility powered by an alternative renewable energy source and with nameplate capacity under 1 MW is exempt for five years after generation begins.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Montana Code Annotated section 15-6-225 exempts machinery and equipment in a qualifying electrical generation facility of less than 1 MW powered by an alternative renewable energy source for five years after generation begins.

eligibleItems: solar energy facilities at least 100 kW
landfill gas facilities at least 100 kW
energy storage resources at least 100 kW after July 18, 2026
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Renewable energy generation facilities pay a nameplate capacity tax of $3,518 per MW in place of personal property tax on depreciable tangible personal property directly used to generate electricity. First-year and changed-capacity periods are prorated by days.
requiredDocuments: Nebraska Department of Revenue nameplate capacity report
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Nebraska law imposes a renewable energy generation facility nameplate capacity tax of $3,518 per MW. Nebraska DOR states the tax is paid in place of personal property tax on depreciable tangible personal property directly used to generate electricity from wind, solar, biomass, or landfill gas. The owner files by March 1 and pays beginning April 1.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: March 1 annual report for the previous calendar year; first payment due April 1 with quarterly payments thereafter.

eligibleItems: renewable energy facilities approved under RETA
energy storage when included in approved renewable facility application
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Nevada's Renewable Energy Tax Abatement program can award an approved partial property tax abatement to eligible renewable energy facilities. Customer-facing savings require the approved abatement agreement, percentage, term, and tax bill.
requiredDocuments: Governor's Office of Energy RETA approval
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: The Nevada Governor's Office of Energy describes RETA as awarding partial sales/use and property tax abatements to eligible renewable energy facilities, subject to application review, hearings, and compliance. The abatement percentage and term must come from the approved project documents.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: The exemption equals the difference between the assessed value of the property with the renewable energy system and the assessed value that would apply without the system, after certification.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: New Jersey Treasury describes the Renewable Energy System Property Tax Exemption as the difference between total assessed value before and after the renewable energy system is installed. Form CRES is used to certify the system, and the exemption is effective for the tax year following certification.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For residential property subject to New Mexico valuation limitation rules, solar energy system installations are excluded from the physical-improvement exception that otherwise could increase valuation outside the cap. Runtime use should require assessor confirmation because leased-system and personal-property treatment may differ.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: New Mexico statutory language in section 7-36-21.2 excludes solar energy system installations from the physical-improvement exception to residential valuation limits. A New Mexico legislative fiscal analysis describes owned residential solar systems as receiving zero valuation treatment, while leased-system treatment may require separate review.

eligibleSectors: utility subject to local opt-out and PILOT rules
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Real property is exempt for fifteen years to the extent of any increase in assessed value attributable to an eligible energy system, unless the taxing jurisdiction has opted out or a PILOT applies.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: New York RPTL 487 exempts the increase in assessed value attributable to eligible energy systems for fifteen years. ORPTS instructions require Form RP-487 to be filed with the assessor by the taxable status date and note local opt-out and PILOT issues.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: File Form RP-487 with the assessor on or before the taxable status date; March 1 in most towns, January 2 in Nassau County, May 1 or June 1 in many Westchester towns, and cities or villages vary.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Eighty percent of the appraised value of a solar energy electric system is excluded from property tax.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: North Carolina General Statutes section 105-275 excludes 80% of the appraised value of a solar energy electric system. NCDOR guidance confirms photovoltaic systems are subject to the 80% exclusion while other property classifications may affect listing.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying solar, wind, or geothermal devices installed to provide heating, cooling, or electrical power may be exempt for five years following installation; only the qualifying portion is exempt when a system also uses another source.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: exempt_value_cents = qualified_device_value_cents for 5 years following installation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: North Dakota Tax Department guidance states that solar, wind, or geothermal device property tax exemptions require a special application by February 1 and can apply for five years after installation. North Dakota Century Code section 57-02-08 limits the exemption to the directly attributable portion if another source is used.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: February 1 of the year for which the exemption is claimed.

eligibleItems: energy facilities with aggregate nameplate capacity of 250 kW or less
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Fixtures and real property included in an energy facility with aggregate nameplate capacity of 250 kW or less are exempt if construction or installation was completed on or after January 1, 2010.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Ohio Revised Code section 5709.53 exempts fixtures and real property included in an energy facility with aggregate nameplate capacity of 250 kW or less if construction or installation was completed on or after January 1, 2010.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualified energy projects may be exempt from public utility tangible personal property tax and associated real property tax treatment if statutory application, certification, and local approval requirements are met. Annual service payments are based on MW and technology, with additional county-approved amounts possible up to the statutory maximum.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if technology == 'solar': base_service_payment_cents = nameplate_mw_in_county * 700000; else: base_service_payment_cents = nameplate_mw_in_county * renewable_payment_rate_cents_per_mw_based_on_ohio_employment_ratio; total_service_payment_cents = min(base_service_payment_cents + county_additional_payment_cents, nameplate_mw_in_county * 900000)
requiredDocuments: Ohio Development qualified energy project application
county resolution or alternative energy zone documentation
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Ohio Revised Code section 5727.75 provides a qualified energy project exemption and service payment structure. Solar projects use a $7,000 per MW base service payment, other renewable projects use statutory rates based on Ohio-domiciled employment ratios, and county resolutions may require additional payments up to $9,000 per MW.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Application to the Director of Development is due by the last day of the tax year preceding the applicable year; annual reports are due before March 1 during and after construction.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: The exemption equals the positive real market value increment created by equipping property with a qualifying alternative energy system. Qualifying systems generally must offset onsite electricity use, be net metering facilities, or satisfy community solar rules.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: ORS 307.175 exempts the positive difference between real market value with and without the qualifying alternative energy system. Oregon Administrative Rule 150-307-0210 limits qualifying personal-consumption systems to those primarily designed to offset onsite use or net metering facilities. The statute does not allow the exemption for tax years beginning after July 1, 2029.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Renewable energy resources and associated equipment used in qualifying residential systems or by qualifying manufacturers are exempt under the cited Rhode Island exemptions.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Rhode Island General Laws section 44-3-3 exempts renewable energy resources used in residential systems and renewable energy resources employed by manufacturers. Municipal assessor confirmation is still required for parcel-level treatment.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For cities and towns that assess tangible tax on commercial renewable energy resources and associated equipment, Rhode Island applies a statewide value/tax formula of $5 per kW AC nameplate for tangible property, subject to exemptions and municipal waiver options.
requiredDocuments: municipal waiver or exemption documentation if applicable
