taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Rhode Island energy regulations and section 44-5-3 provide a $5 per kW AC nameplate treatment for commercial renewable energy systems subject to tangible property taxation, with municipal administration and waiver/exemption issues still relevant.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For renewable resource property under 5 MW, the exemption is the greater of $50,000 of assessed value or 70% of assessed value, not exceeding total assessed value. Geothermal has shorter statutory duration limits.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: South Dakota DOR guidance for renewable resource property under 5 MW states the exemption is the greater of 70% of assessed value or $50,000, no application is needed, and geothermal property has shorter residential and commercial duration limits.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: No application required according to South Dakota DOR guidance; taxpayer should contact local Director of Equalization.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Commercial wind farms and solar facilities at least 5,000 kW pay an alternative tax consisting of a nameplate capacity tax plus a production tax. Annual reports and taxes are due February 1.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: nameplate_tax_cents = nameplate_kw * 300; if technology == 'solar': production_tax_cents = produced_kwh * 0.09; else if technology == 'wind_after_2015': production_tax_cents = produced_kwh * 0.045; annual_tax_cents = nameplate_tax_cents + production_tax_cents
requiredDocuments: South Dakota DOR renewable energy facility report
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: South Dakota law and DOR guidance require commercial wind and solar facilities of at least 5,000 kW to pay alternative taxes. DOR guidance lists a $3.00 per kW nameplate tax and production tax rates of $0.00045 per kWh for newer wind and $0.00090 per kWh for solar, with reports and taxes due February 1.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: February 1 annual report and tax due date.

eligibleItems: nuclear facilities where certified under current clean energy definition
energy storage where part of certified facility
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Certified green energy production facility property may receive special initial valuation treatment. Official Tennessee materials identify a 12.5% of total installed cost cap for solar sourced property when certification is on file; other technologies require current Comptroller/SBE confirmation before modeling.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if technology == 'solar' and certification_on_file: initial_value_cents = min(ordinary_initial_value_cents, round(0.125 * total_installed_cost_cents)); else: unsupported_tax_model_until_current_sbe_formula_confirmed
requiredDocuments: TDEC green energy production facility certification
Comptroller or State Board of Equalization valuation schedule
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Tennessee TDEC describes certification for Green Energy Production Facilities. Tennessee Comptroller solar schedule materials state that solar sourced property values should not initially exceed 12.5% of total installed cost when certification is on file. Non-solar formulas need current SBE confirmation before runtime inclusion.

eligibleItems: onsite solar energy storage and distribution equipment
onsite wind energy storage and distribution equipment
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: A person is entitled to an exemption for the amount of appraised real property value arising from installation or construction of a solar or wind-powered energy device primarily for onsite energy production and distribution, and for the appraised value of a qualifying device owned by the person and installed on real property primarily for onsite use.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Texas Tax Code section 11.27 provides an exemption for the appraised value of qualifying solar or wind-powered energy devices used primarily for onsite production and distribution. The Comptroller lists the Solar and Wind-Powered Energy Device exemption and publishes Form 50-123.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Solar renewable energy plants below 50 kW are exempt from the uniform capacity tax and related fixture/personal property tax. Solar plants at or above the threshold pay $4.00 per kW annually. Grid-connected standalone storage facilities below 600 kWh are exempt, and facilities at or above 600 kWh pay $0.50 per kWh annually. Land remains separately taxable.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if solar_capacity_kw < 50: annual_uniform_capacity_tax_cents = 0; else: annual_uniform_capacity_tax_cents = solar_capacity_kw * 400; if standalone_storage_energy_rating_kwh >= 600: annual_storage_capacity_tax_cents = storage_energy_rating_kwh * 50; else: annual_storage_capacity_tax_cents = 0
requiredDocuments: uniform capacity tax filing or bill
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Vermont statute imposes a $4.00 per kW uniform capacity tax on commissioned solar renewable energy plants and a $0.50 per kWh tax on grid-connected standalone storage facilities, with exemptions below 50 kW solar and below 600 kWh storage. The tax is due April 15 and applies to fixtures and personal property, not land.

eligibleSectors: residential if statutory category and local administration support exemption
taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Virginia exempts certified solar energy equipment and facilities and energy storage systems under pollution-control classification rules. For certain larger solar and storage projects, exemption percentage depends on capacity, application date, and whether the locality has adopted an energy revenue share ordinance.
taxRuleRecords.formulaExpression: if revenue_share_ordinance_applies: exempt_value_cents = qualified_project_value_cents; else if project_capacity_mw > 5 and project_capacity_mw < 150: exempt_value_cents = qualified_project_value_cents * applicable_phase_percentage_decimal; else: exempt_value_cents = qualified_project_value_cents
requiredDocuments: Virginia Energy certification application or certification
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Virginia Code section 58.1-3660 classifies solar energy equipment and facilities and energy storage systems as exempt pollution control property when certified. The broader article provides capacity-specific exemption percentages and local revenue-share interactions, with a July 1, 2030 application cutoff for specified larger projects.
taxRuleRecords.filingDeadline: Application with locality before July 1, 2030 for specified larger solar and storage projects.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Qualifying energy systems are exempt from general property taxes, excluding equipment or components present as part of a conventional energy system.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Wisconsin Statutes section 70.111(18) exempts biogas, synthetic gas, solar, and wind energy systems from general property taxes. Wisconsin DOR Form PR-303 instructs taxpayers to submit the claim to the local assessor by March 1 and excludes conventional energy system components.

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For eligible tax class 1, 2, or 4 New York City properties with DOB approval, annual SEGS abatement for service start dates from 2024-01-01 through 2035-01-01 is the lowest of 7.5% of solar installation costs, annual property taxes, or $62,500; the abatement is applied for four years beginning July 1 after DOB approval. Exclude properties receiving ICAP, 421-a, 421-b, 421-g, or PILOT benefits. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until DOB approval, eligible cost basis, property tax amount, and conflicting-benefit status are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: NYC DOF states that DOB determines eligibility and approves the solar abatement application, DOF administers the benefit, eligible tax classes are 1, 2, and 4, and properties receiving ICAP, 421-a, 421-b, 421-g, or PILOT benefits are ineligible. DOF lists the 2024-01-01 through 2035-01-01 benefit as 7.5% of installation costs, capped by annual property taxes and $62,500, applied for four years. The NYC adopted rule states that the solar and electric energy storage abatement rule became effective June 6, 2024 and that the end date was extended to systems placed in service on or before January 1, 2036. ([New York City Government][6])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For eligible clean-energy systems under RPTL §487, exempt the increase in assessed value attributable to the eligible energy system for 15 years; savings require the assessor-determined incremental assessed value and current property tax lines. NYC DOF states that NYC has determined it will not require a PILOT for energy storage systems at this time. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until exemption approval, incremental assessed value, property-tax rate lines, and any PILOT/opt-out facts are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: NYC DOF describes the RPTL §487 clean-energy exemption as relieving property owners of tax increases directly resulting from eligible systems for 15 years and lists solar, wind, farm-waste, micro-hydroelectric, fuel cell, micro-combined heat and power, and electric energy storage systems. RPTL §487 exempts eligible energy systems from taxation to the extent of increased value attributable to the system for 15 years and permits local opt-out and PILOT treatment in defined cases. ([New York City Government][7])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying residential solar or geothermal devices under Howard County Code §20.128A, credit is the lesser of 50% of eligible costs, $5,000 for a heating or electric generating system, or $1,500 for a hot water system. Credit in any year cannot exceed County property tax, and excess may be carried forward for two additional years. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until timely filing, certification, eligible cost, current County property-tax liability, and carryforward facts are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Howard County's official application cites Howard County Code §20.128A and Maryland §9-203, states that the credit applies to County tax on a residential structure using solar or geothermal devices, and specifies the lesser of 50% eligible costs, $5,000 for heating or electric generation, or $1,500 for hot water; it also states the June 30 filing deadline, annual tax-liability cap, and two-year carryforward. ([Howard County][8])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For approved Howard County high-performance buildings under County Code §20.129B: Core & Shell v2.0 or New Construction v2.2 credits equal 25% of total County property tax for Silver, 50% for Gold, and 75% for Platinum, for five years; Existing Buildings v2.0 credits equal 10% for Silver, 25% for Gold, and 50% for Platinum, for three years. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until rating, property-tax line, filing deadline, and approval are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Howard County's official high-performance-building application cites Maryland §9-242 and Howard County Code §20.129B, states that the credit is against County property taxes, lists the Silver/Gold/Platinum percentages and five-year or three-year periods by rating system, and requires filing by April 1 before the first taxable year. ([Howard County][9])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For an existing eligible energy-efficient building, Energy Reduction Tax Credit percentage for two years equals the improved 12-month ENERGY STAR score minus the baseline 12-month score, multiplied by the code-specified multiplier for the improved score range. If simultaneously approved, add Building Sustainability Tax Credit equal to 25% of property tax owed for LEED O+M Gold, BREEAM In-Use Excellent, or equivalent, or 50% for LEED O+M Platinum, BREEAM In-Use Outstanding, or equivalent; add 10% for qualifying Equity Emphasis Area buildings. Annual credit cannot exceed 100% of annual County property tax liability and countywide annual awards cannot exceed $5 million. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until official application approval, tax liability, ENERGY STAR documentation, rating documentation, and funding-cap status are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Montgomery County Code §52-103A authorizes an Energy Reduction Tax Credit for existing energy-efficient buildings based on baseline and improved ENERGY STAR scores, allows added Building Sustainability and Equity Emphasis Area credits, caps any annual credit at 100% of annual County property tax liability, and limits total annual awards under the section to $5 million. ([American Legal Publishing][10])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Solar and geothermal energy device credits are suspended for applications received after 2012-11-08 and should calculate $0 unless a grandfathered contract/application record is provided. For eligible owner-occupied residential energy conservation devices, office-use credit amount is limited to $250 per property; the credit cannot exceed County property tax and is subject to a $100,000 countywide fiscal-year cap. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until current application acceptance, owner-occupied status, device receipts, and funding availability are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Montgomery County's current application states that solar and geothermal credits were suspended effective November 8, 2011 and are not granted for applications received after November 8, 2012; it defines energy conservation devices, requires receipts and certification, lists a $250-per-property energy conservation device limit, states the credit cannot exceed County property tax on owner-occupied residential property, and lists a $100,000 annual funding limit for energy conservation devices. ([Montgomery County Assets][11])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying buildings in Prince George's County, County real property tax credit equals: new construction or major renovation, Silver 25% for 5 years, Gold 50% for 5 years, Platinum/Emerald 75% for 5 years; existing buildings, Silver 10% for 3 years, Gold 25% for 3 years, Platinum 50% for 3 years. Credits are limited to the County portion of real property tax and subject to a $5 million annual first-come, first-served program cap. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until certification, County tax line, application approval, and cap availability are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Prince George's County's official Finance page states that the credit reduces County real property taxes for buildings with recognized green-building certifications, lists percentage and duration by project type and certification level, requires application by October 1 of the first requested tax year, and notes a $5 million annual first-come, first-served cap. ([Prince George's County][12])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For approved high-performance buildings under Anne Arundel County Code §4-2-311, credit lasts five taxable years beginning in the approval year and applies to building taxes, not land. Residential: Silver 40% capped at $1,000 per certified building, Gold 60% capped at $2,000, Platinum/Emerald 80% capped at $3,000. Commercial: Silver 40% capped at $20,000, Gold 60% capped at $40,000, Platinum/Emerald 80% capped at $60,000. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until SDAT assessment classification, County tax on building, certification, and approval are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Anne Arundel County's tax-credit page lists a High Performance Building Property Tax Credit authorized by Maryland §9-242. The County applications include Code §4-2-311, require filing by June 1, state the credit applies to building taxes and not land for five years, and list residential and commercial percentage caps by LEED/NGBS rating level. ([Anne Arundel County Government][13])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying residential solar energy equipment under Anne Arundel County Code §4-2-315, one-time credit against County real property taxes on the dwelling, not land, equals the lesser of 50% of material and installation/construction cost less federal grants, state grants, and state solar tax credits, or $2,500. Application must be filed by June 1 before the taxable year sought and only once for the credit duration. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until cost net of grants/credits, tax liability, timely filing, and approval are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Anne Arundel County's official solar application includes Code §4-2-315, defines solar energy equipment, states that a one-time credit applies to residential dwellings using solar devices, and calculates the credit as the lesser of 50% of cost net of federal and state grants or state solar credits, or $2,500; the application requires receipts and filing by June 1. ([Anne Arundel County Government][14])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying residential geothermal energy devices under Anne Arundel County Code §4-2-310, one-time credit against County real property taxes on the dwelling, not land, equals the lesser of 50% of material and installation/construction cost less federal grants, state grants, and state geothermal tax credits, or $2,500. Application must be filed by June 1 before the taxable year sought and only once for the credit duration. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until cost net of grants/credits, tax liability, timely filing, and approval are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Anne Arundel County's official geothermal application includes Code §4-2-310, defines qualifying geothermal energy devices as ground-loop heating or cooling devices, states that a one-time credit applies to residential dwellings, and calculates the credit as the lesser of 50% of cost net of federal and state grants or state geothermal tax credits, or $2,500. ([Anne Arundel County Government][15])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For qualifying Fairfax County residential or commercial solar energy equipment, exemption is converted to a tax credit deducted from the real estate bill for five years. Annual credit is computed from the certified exemption value divided by 100 and multiplied by the applicable real estate tax rate. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until Fairfax DTA/LDS approval letter, certified exemption value, and tax-bill rate are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Fairfax County states that qualifying solar equipment is open to residential and commercial properties, is entitled to a five-year tax exemption, requires plans, specifications, drawings, narrative, installed cost documentation, and permit application, and provides an example converting exemption value to annual savings by dividing by 100 and multiplying by the tax rate. ([Fairfax County][16])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For certified Arlington County solar energy equipment, annual credit equals assessor-determined equipment value multiplied by the real estate tax rate per $100 of assessed value, deducted from the real estate tax bill for five years beginning January 1 following approval. County Code §20-9 wholly exempts solar facilities of 25 kW or less. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until Building Official certification, assessor value, rate, and tax-bill application are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Arlington County describes a Solar Exemption Tax Credit under Virginia Code §58.1-3661 and Arlington Code §20-9, with certification by the Building Official, valuation by the Assessor, and annual deduction for five years beginning the following January 1. Arlington Code §20-9 states the exemption is the local tax rate applied to equipment value and subtracted from real property tax or machinery and tools tax, and that facilities of 25 kW or less are wholly exempt. ([Arlington County][17])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For Loudoun County certified solar energy equipment, exemption reduces taxable real estate value by all or part of the solar system value. Residential systems up to 25 kW receive 100% of system value during years in service. Residential systems over 25 kW and less than 5 MW, and commercial systems up to 5 MW, receive 80% of system value for the first five years, 70% for the second five years, and 60% for remaining years. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until county certification, system value, size tier, tax rate, and tax-bill treatment are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Loudoun County states that certified solar equipment is wholly or partially exempt by reducing taxable real estate value, that certification is by the Department of Building and Development, and lists amount/duration tiers by DC system size for residential and commercial systems, along with required application materials. ([Loudoun County][18])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: For Prince William County approved solar energy equipment, the five-year annual credit is based on certified purchase price and installation cost and calculated using the base real estate tax rate only; special levies and fees are excluded. Example formula: annual credit equals certified value divided by 100 multiplied by base real estate tax rate. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until certification, purchase/install cost, base rate, and tax-bill application are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Prince William County states that the exemption is available for all property types, begins January 1 after approval, lasts five years, is based on certified purchase price and installation, uses the base real estate tax rate only, excludes special levies and fees, and requires submission to Development Services. The county code excerpt states that the exemption is 100% of the value applied against real estate property tax and is effective for five years. ([Prince William County Government][19])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Cincinnati residential CRA abatement generally exempts 100% of eligible increased taxable value from qualifying new construction or remodeling up to the applicable maximum abated improvement value and term determined by ordinance, construction date, construction type, neighborhood tier, and certifications/bonuses. Environmental certifications such as LEED or Living Building Challenge can increase term or capped value under the City's rules. Hamilton County Auditor determines the abated improvement value and commencement. Customer-facing savings default to $0 until the City approval, Auditor value, neighborhood tier/map, certification, cap, term, and tax-bill treatment are confirmed.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Cincinnati states that its residential tax abatement lets owners pay taxes on pre-improvement value for up to 15 years and that increased valuation is determined by the Hamilton County Auditor. The City's rules state that the RTA program incentivizes sustainable development, is authorized by Ordinance 106-2023, defines improvements as work that increases value according to Hamilton County Auditor assessment, uses tiered neighborhood incentives for projects commencing on or after September 1, 2023, and allows environmental certification bonuses for LEED and Living Building Challenge. ([DCEDChooseCincy][20])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Cincinnati commercial CRA abatements can provide partial real-property-tax abatement up to 67% net for up to 15 years for eligible commercial, industrial, mixed-use, or five-plus-unit residential projects; the City notes the program can incentivize green building. A CRA agreement must be signed before construction, Council approval is required, and school-board PILOT requirements apply. Customer-facing savings must remain $0 unless an executed project-specific agreement and tax lines are available.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Cincinnati states that commercial CRA incentives may provide a maximum 67% net property tax abatement for up to 15 years, can incentivize green building, require applications to be reviewed and approved by City Council, and require a CRA agreement before construction. Ohio law requires commercial or industrial CRA exemptions to be governed by a written agreement entered into before construction or remodeling. ([DCEDChooseCincy][21])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: State business tax model for business_and_occupation_tax, gross_receipts_tax, business_tax_rate_preference.
State business tax model for corporate_income_tax, franchise_tax, minimum_franchise_tax.
State business tax model for corporate_income_tax, business_tax_credit.
State business tax model for property_tax, state_education_tax, local_income_tax, renaissance_zone_tax_exemption.
State business tax model for corporate_income_tax, minimum_business_corporation_tax.
State business tax model for commercial_activity_tax, gross_receipts_tax.
State business tax model for corporate_excise_tax, corporate_income_tax, corporate_activity_tax, gross_receipts_tax.
State business tax model for franchise_tax, margin_tax, gross_receipts_based_tax.
State business tax model for commerce_tax, gross_receipts_tax.
State business tax model for corporate_income_tax, franchise_tax, gross_receipts_tax, business_license_tax.
State business tax model for franchise_tax, excise_tax, business_tax, gross_receipts_tax.
State business tax model for corporate_income_tax, limited_liability_entity_tax, gross_receipts_based_tax.
State business tax model for corporate_franchise_tax, business_income_base_tax, business_capital_base_tax, fixed_dollar_minimum_tax, manufacturer_rate_preference.

Everett B&O tax = Everett taxable gross receipts multiplied by the applicable city B&O rate. Current ordinary city rate source states 0.1% or 0.001; local special taxes such as utility, gambling, and admissions taxes are separate activities and must not be assumed unless the taxpayer profile matches.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Everett states city B&O tax is based on gross receipts and the present tax rate is 0.1% or 0.001 multiplied by Everett gross receipts; Everett also publishes Schedule C for Multiple Activities Tax Credit calculations. ([Everett WA][60])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Seattle B&O/business license tax = taxable gross revenue by Seattle classification minus any source-backed deductions, multiplied by the applicable classification rate; beginning January 1, 2026, the general business license tax threshold increases to $2,000,000, but businesses below the threshold still file and report $0 tax due.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Seattle states businesses must obtain a license tax certificate, file B&O/business license tax returns, and pay tax if due; classification rates vary by business activity. Seattle Director's Rule 5-013 states the business license tax threshold increases from $100,000 to $2,000,000 beginning January 1, 2026, while under-threshold businesses still file and report $0 tax due. Seattle also publishes 2025-2026 license fee tiers. ([Seattle][61])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Los Angeles business tax generally equals in-city/apportioned gross receipts by LAMC classification multiplied by the applicable rate per $1,000 of gross receipts, with minimums, exemptions, and renewal timing rules applied from the current City Finance schedule.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Los Angeles Finance publishes business tax rates by classification, including rates per $1,000 of gross receipts for contractors, services, professional occupations, rentals, retail, and wholesale. The City states most business taxes are based on gross receipts, renewals require reporting tax measure by activity, and apportionment must reflect gross receipts earned from engaging in business in Los Angeles. The small-business exemption depends on global gross receipts and timely renewal. ([Los Angeles Office of Finance][62])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: San Francisco gross receipts tax requires determining the taxpayer's business activity category or categories, San Francisco gross receipts, and applying the rate schedules and exemptions for the tax year; related annual filing may also include homelessness gross receipts tax, commercial rents tax, overpaid executive gross receipts tax, administrative office tax, and registration fees when applicable.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: San Francisco Treasurer states gross receipts tax rates vary by San Francisco gross receipts and business activity category and provides steps to determine the category and San Francisco gross receipts. Annual filing instructions list business registration renewal plus, if applicable, gross receipts tax, homelessness gross receipts tax, commercial rents tax, overpaid executive gross receipts tax, and administrative office tax. Proposition M increased the gross receipts and overpaid executive small-business exemption ceiling to $5 million starting tax year 2025. ([Treasurer & Tax Collector][63])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Burbank business license tax generally equals the applicable flat/basic tax plus the applicable employee levy and administrative fees; certain business categories use different structures. Use only current adopted fee schedules for the runtime tax year.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Burbank states most businesses pay an initial business tax fee consisting of an application fee, flat tax, and employee levy, while certain business types use different structures. Retrieved FY 2025-26 fee schedule rows include a business tax registration fee, state accessibility fee, zoning review fee, and category rows such as manufacturing/wholesale/retail with a basic annual amount and employee levy. Because the research date is in FY 2026-27, current-year fee confirmation is required before user-facing calculation. ([City of Burbank][64])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Pasadena business license tax generally equals the fixed/basic license amount for the taxpayer's business category plus employee, professional, machine, unit, or other add-on amounts listed in the adopted schedule of taxes, fees, and charges for the fiscal year.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Pasadena publishes adopted FY 2027 fee and tax schedules. The FY 2027 schedule lists business license tax rows such as general business basic tax plus per-employee amount, take-out service basic tax plus per-employee amount, and professional license amounts for the first professional, additional professionals, and nonprofessional employees. ([City of Pasadena][65])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Anaheim business license tax is calculated by category. Retrieved FY 2026-27 proposed schedule rows include gross-receipts rates per $1,000 for manufacturing, wholesale, retail, hotel/motel, entertainment, miscellaneous and other categories, plus non-gross-receipts formulas such as professional owner/partner/officer amounts, apartment unit counts, and nonresidential rental square footage. Use only after confirming adopted FY 2026-27 schedule status.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Anaheim FY 2026-27 proposed fee schedule includes business license tax rows using gross-receipts rates per $1,000 for manufacturing/wholesale/retail, hotel/motel, entertainment, miscellaneous, telephone, and coin-operated activities, as well as professional, apartment, and nonresidential rental formulas. Adopted-schedule confirmation is required before user-facing calculation. ([Anaheim][66])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: San Diego Business Tax Certificate fee generally equals $34 for businesses with 12 or fewer employees, or $125 plus $5 per employee for businesses with 13 or more employees, plus applicable state and local add-on fees such as the SB-1186 fee and minimum wage enforcement fee when current instructions require them.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: San Diego Treasurer lists annual Business Tax Certificate rates of $34 for 12 or fewer employees and $125 plus $5 per employee for 13 or more employees. San Diego states all businesses operating in the city must obtain a Business Tax Certificate and identifies additional fees including the SB-1186 state fee and, beginning July 1, 2025, a minimum wage enforcement fee per employee. ([San Diego][67])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Vernon hazardous waste business license tax equals 4% of annual gross receipts from inorganic hazardous waste treatment, storage, or disposal and 1% of annual gross receipts from organic or infectious waste treatment, storage, or disposal, with a $5,000 minimum per calendar year. Related corporate entity hazardous waste treatment is taxed at $0.30 per gallon with a $5,000 minimum; waste-to-energy business is taxed at $0.85 per ton of incoming material.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Vernon code states hazardous waste treatment, storage, or disposal tax rates of 4% of annual gross receipts for inorganic waste and 1% for organic or infectious waste, each subject to a $5,000 minimum, and separately states related-entity hazardous waste and waste-to-energy measures. Vernon also states businesses moving into the city must obtain a Certificate of Occupancy and Business License before moving employees or equipment. ([eCode360][68])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Vernon warehouse license tax from retrieved official agenda material: warehouse businesses with 5,000 square feet or less pay $1,200; warehouse businesses with 5,001 square feet or more pay $0.21 per square foot, with a maximum tax of $11,950. Confirm current codified rate before calculation.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Vernon official agenda material lists warehouse business license fees of $1,200 for 5,000 square feet or less and $0.21 per square foot for 5,001 square feet or more, capped at $11,950, but the retrieved source is an agenda packet rather than the codified municipal code. ([City of Vernon][69])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Detroit corporate income tax generally equals Detroit taxable corporate income multiplied by the Detroit corporate income tax rate; 2025 instructions state the rate is 2.0%. Corporations with annual Detroit CIT liability over $250 must make quarterly estimated payments.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Detroit states the business income tax rate is 2.00% for businesses. Michigan Treasury's Detroit CIT materials state corporations doing business in Detroit must file an annual return, 2025 Form 5297 instructions state the Detroit corporate income tax rate is 2.0%, and 2025 forms include quarterly estimates for corporations with liability over $250. ([City of Detroit][70])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Philadelphia BIRT has two components: gross receipts tax and net income tax. Tax year 2025 rates are 1.410 mills on gross receipts and 5.71% on taxable net income; tax year 2026 rates announced by the City are 1.395 mills on gross receipts and 5.65% on taxable net income for returns filed and paid in 2027.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Philadelphia states BIRT has gross receipts and taxable net income components. City guidance lists tax year 2025 rates of 1.410 mills on gross receipts and 5.71% on taxable net income, and later City guidance states tax year 2026 rates will be 1.395 mills and 5.65% for returns filed and paid in 2027. ([City of Philadelphia][71])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Portland-area business income tax stack may include Portland Business License Tax at 2.6% of adjusted net income, Multnomah County Business Income Tax at 2.0% of net income, and Metro Supportive Housing Services business income tax at 1.0% of profits for businesses above the Metro gross receipts threshold. Apply only to confirmed jurisdictions and tax bases.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Portland Revenue lists City Business License Tax at 2.6%, Multnomah County Business Income Tax at 2%, and Metro SHS business income tax at 1%. Portland Code section 7.02.500 states the City tax is 2.6% of adjusted net income. Multnomah County states MCBIT is 2% of net income. Metro states SHS is funded by a 1% business income tax on net income or profits for businesses above the $5 million gross receipts threshold. ([Portland.gov][72])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: New York City Business Corporation Tax requires calculating the applicable business income base tax, capital base tax, or fixed dollar minimum tax and paying the required amount under NYC rules; rates depend on taxpayer type, including qualified manufacturing corporation, small business, financial corporation, or other taxpayer.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: NYC Finance lists Business Corporation Tax business income base rates, including qualified manufacturing corporations, small businesses, financial corporations, and remaining taxpayers, and also publishes fixed dollar minimum tax bands based on NYC receipts. ([New York City Government][73])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: New York City UBT generally equals 4% of unincorporated business taxable income allocated to New York City, reduced by applicable full or partial UBT credit when eligible.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: NYC Finance states the Unincorporated Business Tax rate is 4% of taxable income allocated to New York City and describes a full credit for liabilities up to $3,400 and partial credit for liabilities from $3,401 to $5,400. ([New York City Government][74])

taxRuleRecords.formulaText: Ohio municipal net profit tax equals municipal taxable net profit allocated or apportioned to a municipality multiplied by that municipality's enacted income tax rate. Centralized filing with the Ohio Department of Taxation is optional for businesses that elect it; otherwise local municipal filing rules apply.
taxRuleRecords.evidenceText: Ohio Department of Taxation states municipal net profit tax is a local income tax levied on business net profits. Dublin's official tax page is an example municipality stating its 2.0% local income tax applies to business and rental net profits and businesses conducting business in Dublin must file a net profit return. Ohio DOR due-date and alert pages describe annual municipal net profit filing timing and centralized filing through state systems. ([Ohio Department of Taxation][75])

localOptionAuthorityRecords.evidenceText: Maryland Tax-Property §9-203 authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant by law a local property tax credit for structures using solar, geothermal, or qualifying energy conservation devices; §9-242 separately authorizes local high-performance-building credits and requires local law to specify amount, duration, criteria, qualifications, and other provisions. ([Maryland General Assembly][1])

Maryland Tax-Property §9-318(f) authorizes Prince George's County, by law, to grant a property tax credit against county property tax on real or personal property owned or leased by a certified green business, and the local law must provide eligibility, certification, amount, duration, and procedures. ([Maryland General Assembly][2])

Virginia Code §58.1-3661 applies only in a county, city, or town that has adopted an ordinance; the local building department certifies eligible equipment, the assessor determines value, and the exemption is computed by applying the local tax rate to the equipment value for a term not less than five years. The Virginia Administrative Code requires the solar exemption application to be made to the local building department and transmitted for assessor valuation. ([Virginia Law][3])

New York RPTL §487 provides a 15-year exemption for eligible energy systems to the extent of the increase in value attributable to the system, but counties, cities, towns, villages, and school districts may opt out by local law or resolution by technology category; non-opt-out taxing jurisdictions may also require a PILOT for solar or wind systems. The New York Tax Department publishes an official opt-out list updated with records on file. ([NYSenate.gov][4])

Ohio CRA authority requires a political subdivision to adopt a resolution describing CRA boundaries and may specify eligible classifications and residential exemption percentages; eligible owners apply for exemption from real property taxation of a percentage of new-structure assessed value or increased assessed value after remodeling. Commercial or industrial exemptions require a written agreement before construction or remodeling. ([Ohio Laws][5])

workflowPatterns.description: Project-, company-, parcel-, or zone-specific abatements such as renaissance zones, enterprise zones, reinvestment zones, and local economic-development abatements. Geography can route a taxpayer to the workflow, but the benefit usually depends on an approved agreement, designation, local resolution, zone boundary, eligible tax lines, and compliance status.
whenToCalculate: An executed official agreement, local ordinance, resolution, designation, or state approval identifies the taxpayer, project, parcel, zone, tax years, eligible property, abatement percentage or phaseout, and eligible tax lines.
The parcel or facility is verified inside the official zone or reinvestment boundary using official legal descriptions, maps, assessor records, or program documents.
The current tax bill or assessor record identifies the ordinary tax lines and values that are eligible for abatement.
Any employment, investment, certification, local approval, reporting, annual certification, or current-on-taxes requirements are confirmed for the relevant tax year.
The model separately stores gross abated tax, realized value, recapture exposure, and unsupported or excluded tax lines.
whenToReturnZero: Only a DSIRE or marketing description is available and no executed agreement, designation, or parcel-specific approval exists.
The parcel or facility boundary cannot be verified against official zone or reinvestment-zone documents.
The program is discretionary and no local-unit approval, public hearing, ordinance, or signed agreement can be confirmed.
The current tax bill does not identify eligible tax lines or the assessor has not confirmed eligible value.
The agreement has expired, been revoked, is in recapture/noncompliance, or the relevant tax year is outside the approved term.
The tax line is explicitly excluded by statute or program documents, such as special assessments, local bond obligations, school sinking fund taxes, or other non-abated charges.
requiredDocuments: Executed abatement, renaissance-zone, enterprise-zone, reinvestment-zone, or economic-development agreement
Local government ordinance, resolution, public-hearing record, or approval minutes
Official zone boundary map, legal description, or parcel list
Assessor valuation record and current tax bill
Annual compliance certification, employment or investment certification, and current-on-taxes confirmation
Recapture, cancellation, amendment, expiration, or phaseout documentation
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Return $0 by default. Include a customer-facing amount only after official project documents, parcel eligibility, eligible tax lines, tax-year timing, and compliance are confirmed. Do not treat a state, county, ZIP, or DSIRE program match as calculable savings.
exampleSourceTypes: County or city ordinance and resolution
Comptroller or state registry of tax abatement agreements

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Michigan Renewable Energy Renaissance Zone benefits apply only to operations of the designated company within geographic boundaries; applications are submitted by the county or distressed community; the city, village, or township must approve an abatement resolution; state education tax, personal and real property taxes, and local income tax may be abated, while federal taxes, local bond obligations, school sinking fund taxes, special assessments, and sales/use tax are not abated; taxes may be abated up to 15 years and phased out over the last three years.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use tax_abatement_or_pilot with needs_program_documentation, needs_tax_bill, needs_assessor_confirmation, and excluded-tax-line handling.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Oregon standard enterprise zones may provide local property-tax abatement for three to five years; qualifying businesses must satisfy employment, first-source, local-condition, and filing requirements; the application must be filed before physical project work, and claims are filed with the county assessor after property is placed in service.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Do not calculate from geography alone; require application timing, zone sponsor approval, assessor filings, and tax-bill inputs.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Oregon long-term rural enterprise zone facilities may be exempt from local property taxes for seven to fifteen years, but certification requires pre-construction application, local sponsor agreement, local resolutions, minimum investment, job creation, compensation, and other criteria.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use a project-specific abatement workflow; require sponsor agreement and certification before any customer-facing savings.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Texas Chapter 312 tax abatement is a local agreement between a taxpayer and taxing unit that exempts increases in property value for up to ten years; cities, counties, and special districts may use it, while school districts may not.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require the executed local agreement and incremental value; do not abate base value or school-district taxes unless a separate source-backed program applies.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Texas Chapter 312 requires local guidelines, public hearing, reinvestment-zone designation, public notice, agreement approval, specific improvements, inspection, recapture provisions, annual certification, and possible cancellation or modification for noncompliance.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Runtime must capture public approval, reinvestment-zone status, improvement-specific eligibility, compliance, recapture, and annual certification.

workflowPatterns.description: Renewable-energy exemptions or abatements with a statutory payment-in-lieu-of-taxes overlay, service payment, or local PILOT contract. These programs can be partly formulaic but still require jurisdiction-specific adoption, opt-out, agreement, or tax-bill confirmation.
whenToCalculate: The statute establishes the exemption or PILOT authority and the local jurisdiction has not opted out or otherwise disqualified the project.
An executed PILOT contract, county service-payment resolution, assessor-approved exemption application, or statutory formula identifies the project and tax years.
Nameplate capacity, taxable status date, placed-in-service date, project type, ownership, and parcel jurisdiction are source-backed and current.
The tax bill or assessor record identifies the tax lines displaced, exempted, or replaced by the PILOT or service payment.
The calculation can distinguish PILOT or service payment due from tax savings.
whenToReturnZero: The local jurisdiction may opt out or require a PILOT, but no official opt-out, PILOT, or approval status is known.
A PILOT is permitted but not executed.
The project has not filed the required exemption application by the taxable-status deadline.
The PILOT amount equals or exceeds the ordinary tax counterfactual.
The required runtime inputs support the PILOT liability but not the ordinary tax counterfactual; in that case, show liability internally and return customer-facing savings as $0.
The statute caps or permits payments but does not supply the project-specific amount.
requiredDocuments: Local opt-out law, resolution, or non-opt-out confirmation
County board resolution or local approval record
Current tax bill with ordinary and PILOT/service-payment lines
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Return $0 unless the local PILOT or service-payment terms and ordinary tax counterfactual are known. If only the PILOT liability is calculable, show it as an internal tax or payment obligation, not customer-facing savings.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: New York RPTL 487 exempts eligible renewable systems from taxation to the extent of the increase in value for fifteen years; owners must file an assessor application by the taxable status date; local jurisdictions and school districts may opt out for specified systems; jurisdictions that have not opted out may require a PILOT contract, and payments cannot exceed the taxes that would otherwise be payable but for the exemption.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require taxable-status filing, local opt-out status, PILOT contract status, and ordinary tax counterfactual.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Massachusetts Clause Forty-fifth exempts certain solar, wind, and co-located storage systems for twenty years if statutory use, size, or PILOT-agreement conditions are met; the municipality may execute a PILOT agreement, and the exemption can include personal property and real property taxes attributable to the system and land when ownership conditions are satisfied.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require ownership/use classification, size, PILOT status, system land treatment, and municipality agreement details.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Ohio law exempts tangible personal property of qualified energy projects using renewable energy resources if statutory conditions are met; for projects of five megawatts or more, county approval may be required; counties may require annual service payments, and the combined service payment cannot exceed nine thousand dollars per megawatt of nameplate capacity in the county.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use county approval, service-payment resolution, nameplate capacity by county, and tax-year exemption status as required runtime inputs.

workflowPatterns.description: Statewide statutory replacement taxes, nameplate-capacity taxes, per-kW valuations, or production taxes for renewable energy systems. These can be calculable as liability when the statutory formula and physical inputs are known, but customer-facing savings require a confirmed ordinary property-tax counterfactual.
whenToCalculate: The statute provides a per-kW, per-kWh, per-MWh, or similar formula and the relevant capacity, production, tax year, property classification, and ownership/use facts are known.
The property components included in the statutory tax are separated from excluded components such as underlying land, non-system improvements, or property below the statutory threshold.
Required annual reports or production reports are available or the statute supplies an official default calculation method.
Assessor or taxing-agency confirmation supports how the statutory tax appears on the tax roll or tax bill.
whenToReturnZero: The model can compute a statutory tax due but does not have a source-backed ordinary ad valorem counterfactual.
The system is below a statutory threshold or exempt, but the avoided tax line cannot be verified.
The formula depends on annual production or capacity reporting and the report is missing.
The system straddles multiple parcels or jurisdictions and capacity or production cannot be allocated.
The statute excludes land or other property, and the runtime record does not separate excluded components.
requiredDocuments: Annual production report or official default production calculation
Tax bill or tax-roll record showing the statutory tax or valuation treatment
Ordinary property-tax counterfactual if savings will be shown
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Statutory liability may be calculated internally when all formula inputs are known. Customer-facing savings remain $0 unless ordinary property-tax liability, statutory liability, eligible property components, and assessor treatment are all confirmed.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Rhode Island cities and towns tax renewable energy resources and associated equipment at five dollars per kilowatt of AC nameplate capacity for tangible property, subject to statutory exceptions.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use property_tax_special_valuation; require AC nameplate capacity, tangible-versus-real property treatment, and municipal assessor confirmation.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Rhode Island exempts residential renewable energy resources and associated equipment after December 31, 2015, and provides a manufacturer-related renewable exemption under the same exemption statute.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require system use and taxpayer classification before applying the per-kW treatment or exemption.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Vermont imposes an annual uniform capacity tax of four dollars per kilowatt of plant capacity for solar renewable energy and fifty cents per kilowatt-hour for certain energy storage facilities of at least six hundred kilowatt-hours; smaller solar plants and smaller storage facilities are exempt, and the statute applies to fixtures and personal property, not the underlying land.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Calculate statutory liability from capacity and threshold status; do not include land or ordinary-property-tax savings without a counterfactual.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Minnesota imposes a solar energy production tax on solar energy generating systems with capacity over one megawatt AC at one dollar and twenty cents per megawatt-hour; systems of one megawatt AC or less are exempt, and missing reports can trigger a Commissioner-determined tax using nameplate capacity and a statutory capacity factor.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require AC capacity, annual MWh, reporting status, and tax administrator certification before calculating liability.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Minnesota imposes a wind energy production tax by system size using cents-per-kilowatt-hour rates; very small systems and some political-subdivision systems are exempt, and missing reports can trigger a Commissioner-determined tax using nameplate capacity and a statutory capacity factor.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require wind-system size classification, kWh production, reporting status, and allocation to jurisdictions.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Minnesota exempts real and personal property of wind energy systems except land, and exempts personal property of solar energy systems while separately classifying real property primarily used for solar energy production.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Separate system property from land and non-system real property before modeling any ordinary-tax counterfactual.

workflowPatterns.description: Property Assessed Clean Energy and similar contractual assessment financing appears on property tax bills but is a financing charge or special assessment, not a tax credit, exemption, abatement, or tax savings mechanism.
whenToCalculate: Do not calculate as tax savings.
A non-savings property-tax-bill adapter may record the current PACE assessment line as a financing cost if the tax bill, administrator record, and assessment amount are present.
A payoff, removal, or correction can be reflected only from the PACE administrator or tax collector record.
whenToReturnZero: Always return customer-facing tax savings as $0 for PACE charges unless a separate, source-backed tax credit or exemption exists outside the PACE financing.
Return $0 when only the existence of PACE financing is known and the current assessment amount or payoff schedule is missing.
Return $0 when a user treats reduced utility cost, loan proceeds, or financed project cost as tax savings.
requiredDocuments: Current secured property tax bill showing the PACE line
Administrator payoff, removal, correction, or lien release documentation
Mortgage escrow or impound statement if cash-flow analysis is requested outside tax savings
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Never include PACE as positive tax savings. Suppress from savings totals and, if needed, show as a separate financing obligation or property-tax-bill charge.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: California law authorizes public agencies to designate areas for voluntary contractual assessments and financing of public improvements, distributed renewable generation, and energy or water efficiency improvements permanently fixed to property; the resolution must describe improvements, boundaries, financing arrangements, and tax-roll consultation.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Classify as contractual-assessment financing, not tax savings.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: San Diego County states that PACE finances energy-efficient improvements through special assessments on the property tax bill; the assessment becomes a lien, remains until paid or removed by the administrator, is collected with property taxes, and can create penalties, interest, foreclosure, or tax sale risk if unpaid.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Treat PACE as a tax-bill charge and lien; no positive savings should be included.

workflowPatterns.description: Direct assessments, benefit assessments, parcel taxes, CFD or Mello-Roos charges, special district charges, and similar tax-bill add-ons may appear beside property taxes but generally are imposed by a levying agency for a property-specific service, debt, or assessment. They should be parsed as tax-bill lines, not modeled as retrofit tax incentives unless a source-backed reduction or exemption specifically applies.
whenToCalculate: Do not calculate as savings by default.
A property-tax adapter may parse and store the current bill line if the tax bill identifies the levying agency and amount.
Calculate a charge only when the levying agency publishes an official formula, parcel applicability rule, and current assessment roll or direct-assessment file.
Calculate savings only if an official exemption, cancellation, refund, or abatement applies to that specific assessment line and the levying agency confirms the parcel eligibility.
whenToReturnZero: The direct assessment is merely present on the tax bill.
The levying agency formula or parcel list is unavailable.
The county tax collector or auditor is only collecting the charge and does not provide the calculation basis.
The assessment is a special district, bond, sewer, lighting, landscaping, fire, vector, solid waste, or similar charge unrelated to the retrofit incentive.
The user supplies a property tax total but does not separate ad valorem taxes from direct assessments.
requiredDocuments: Current secured tax bill with direct assessment lines
Levying agency resolution, ordinance, engineer report, or rate schedule
County direct-assessment roll or submission file if available
Official exemption, cancellation, or correction record if savings is claimed
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Return $0 unless an official levying-agency source confirms a parcel-specific exemption, cancellation, or reduction and the current bill line is verified. Do not net direct assessments against ad valorem property-tax savings without line-level support.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Los Angeles County states that direct assessments are shown separately on the secured property tax bill and added to ad valorem taxes; the Auditor-Controller places the assessment on the bill and distributes collections to the levying agency, while calculation questions go to the agency or city.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use tax-bill parsing and levying-agency confirmation; do not infer a savings formula from the county bill alone.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Los Angeles County describes the property tax bill as consisting of taxes, debt service, and direct assessments, with direct assessments being property-specific.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Separate ad valorem taxes, debt service, and direct assessments before calculating any retrofit tax benefit.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Los Angeles County explains that special districts annually provide parcel lists and assessment amounts or resolutions, and if requirements are met the Auditor places the special assessment on the tax bill.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Require the special district or levying agency source for calculation rather than inventing the assessment formula.

workflowPatterns.description: Economic-development programs may include grants, loans, discounted services, infrastructure commitments, or reimbursements that are economically valuable but are not tax credits, exemptions, abatements, special valuations, or PILOTs. These should not be included in tax savings unless the official agreement directly reduces or replaces an eligible tax liability.
whenToCalculate: Do not calculate in the tax-savings engine unless the agreement explicitly changes a tax liability and identifies the tax type, eligible base, formula, term, and taxpayer.
If the agreement is a grant, loan, in-kind service, reimbursement, infrastructure contribution, or utility-rate concession, route to a non-tax incentive workflow outside this schema.
If the agreement contains both tax and non-tax components, model only the tax component and suppress non-tax amounts from tax savings.
whenToReturnZero: The opportunity is described as a grant, loan, service, discounted infrastructure, development reimbursement, or utility concession without a tax-line reduction.
The official agreement is unavailable or does not identify the taxpayer and tax effect.
The program is discretionary and the taxpayer has not been awarded or approved.
The amount depends on post-performance reimbursement, appropriation, or compliance not yet certified.
workflowPatterns.customerFacingPolicy: Return $0 for tax savings unless a source-backed tax component exists. Non-tax grants or loans may be displayed only in a separate non-tax incentive category.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Texas Chapter 380 and 381 programs allow municipalities or counties to offer loans, grants, and services at little or no cost to promote economic development; these programs are reported to the Comptroller, but they are not automatically property tax abatements.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Classify grants and services as non-tax unless an agreement separately identifies a source-backed tax abatement or tax reduction.

sourceBackedFacts.evidenceText: Texas maintains a searchable database for economic development and tax abatement agreements, with reporting requirements for Chapter 380, Chapter 381, and Chapter 312 agreements.
sourceBackedFacts.modelImpact: Use official registries to verify whether a local agreement is tax-related, non-tax, active, and taxpayer-specific.

matchSignals: host community payment tied to property tax
statutory annual payment replacing property tax
requiredEvidence: Official statute or local ordinance authorizing the PILOT
Executed agreement, county resolution, or required notice and acceptance record
Eligible tax lines and ordinary tax counterfactual
doNotInfer: Do not infer a PILOT amount from the word PILOT alone.
Do not treat a PILOT payment due as savings.
Do not assume local adoption where the statute allows opt-out, opt-in, or discretionary agreement.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: New York allows local jurisdictions that did not opt out of the renewable exemption to require a PILOT contract, but the payment cannot exceed the taxes that would otherwise be payable.
Ohio qualified energy project service payments can be required by county resolution and are capped by nameplate capacity.

requiredEvidence: Eligible tax lines and excluded tax lines
Current tax bill or assessor valuation
doNotInfer: Do not calculate from state eligibility alone.
Do not calculate from a zone map unless the taxpayer has the required approval.
Do not include special assessments, bond obligations, or excluded taxes unless the source expressly abates them.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: Michigan RERZ benefits apply only to designated company operations within approved boundaries and require local abatement resolution and state approval.
Texas Chapter 312 requires local guidelines, public hearing, reinvestment-zone designation, agreement approval, specific improvements, annual certification, and recapture provisions.
Oregon enterprise-zone benefits require application before physical work and later claims with the county assessor.

requiredEvidence: Ordinary tax counterfactual if savings is shown
doNotInfer: Do not convert statutory tax due into savings without ordinary property-tax counterfactual.
Do not apply a per-kW rate to land or non-system improvements unless the statute includes them.
Do not use DC capacity where the statute requires AC capacity.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: Rhode Island uses a per-kW AC nameplate-capacity treatment for renewable energy resources and associated equipment.
Vermont imposes a uniform capacity tax on qualifying solar and storage property and excludes the underlying land from that tax treatment.
Minnesota solar production tax depends on capacity threshold, annual production, and reporting or official default determination.

matchSignals: energy efficiency assessment on tax bill
requiredEvidence: Payoff or removal record if applicable
doNotInfer: Do not treat financed project proceeds as tax savings.
Do not treat the tax-bill placement of PACE as a tax exemption or credit.
Do not offset PACE charges against tax benefits unless a separate source-backed tax incentive exists.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: San Diego County describes PACE as financing through a special assessment on the property tax bill that becomes a lien and is collected with property taxes.
California statutory PACE authority is framed as voluntary contractual assessments and financing for improvements.

requiredEvidence: Official levy formula or parcel assessment roll
Official exemption or cancellation if savings is claimed
doNotInfer: Do not include direct assessments in ordinary ad valorem property-tax savings.
Do not use county tax-collector totals without separating direct assessments from ad valorem taxes and debt service.
Do not calculate a reduction unless the levying agency confirms the parcel-specific treatment.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: Los Angeles County states direct assessments are shown separately on the secured tax bill and added to ad valorem taxes, and calculation questions belong to the levying agency.

matchSignals: revenue sharing not tied to tax liability
requiredEvidence: Proof that the benefit is a tax-line reduction if tax modeling is requested
doNotInfer: Do not include non-tax grants, loans, or services in tax savings.
Do not transform a reimbursement into a tax credit unless an official tax agency source says it is one.
Do not include discretionary awards before approval and compliance certification.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: Texas Chapter 380 and 381 programs may provide loans, grants, and services at little or no cost, which are not automatically tax abatements.

matchSignals: valueModelKind not in RetroFi supported model kinds
requiredEvidence: Official source for formula or agreement
doNotInfer: Do not calculate from unsupported valueModelKind labels such as tax_exempt_liability or tax_rate_difference unless remapped to a supported model kind with sources.
Do not surface customer-facing savings while model repair is pending.

sourceBackedRationale.evidenceText: The provided RetroFi framework requires unsupported_tax_model, source_unavailable, or needs_* statuses where a tax area cannot be verified or modeled, and customer-facing savings must be zero unless formula, jurisdiction, source confidence, and runtime inputs support inclusion.

unsupportedPatterns.description: PACE financing, contractual clean-energy assessments, and assessment liens are not positive tax savings.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: The charge is financing collected on the tax bill, not a tax reduction.
requiredReviewToReclassify: Separate source-backed tax credit, exemption, or abatement unrelated to PACE financing
Tax bill line and administrator record if shown as financing cost

unsupportedPatterns.description: Direct assessments, parcel charges, special district charges, and special taxes should not be used as retrofit tax savings without a line-specific exemption or cancellation.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: The county bill may show the line, but the levying agency controls the calculation and any exemption.

unsupportedPatterns.description: A generic PILOT authority, DSIRE listing, or local-option statute is not enough to calculate customer-facing savings.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: PILOT amounts and tax effects are taxpayer-, parcel-, jurisdiction-, or agreement-specific.

unsupportedPatterns.description: Being in a county, city, enterprise zone, renaissance zone, or reinvestment zone is only a routing fact unless official project approval and taxpayer compliance are verified.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: Zone benefits are often discretionary, application-based, agreement-based, time-limited, and compliance-dependent.

unsupportedPatterns.description: A statutory per-kW, per-MWh, or production tax may be calculable as liability but not as savings unless ordinary ad valorem tax is also known.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: Savings require the difference between ordinary tax and statutory tax, and the ordinary tax counterfactual is usually assessor-specific.
requiredReviewToReclassify: Assessor confirmation of included and excluded property components

unsupportedPatterns.description: Economic-development grants, loans, no-cost services, utility concessions, and infrastructure reimbursements are not tax savings unless an official source identifies a tax liability reduction.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: The value may be economically relevant but is outside the tax calculation model.
requiredReviewToReclassify: Agreement section identifying a tax type and tax-line reduction
Tax agency or local government source confirming treatment
Separate accounting of tax and non-tax components

unsupportedPatterns.description: Local-option incentives, negotiated abatements, utility tax substitutes, special assessment reductions, or obsolete program pages should be suppressed when official local adoption, current ordinance text, agreement records, or tax-bill treatment cannot be verified.
unsupportedPatterns.returnZeroReason: RetroFi must not invent local adoptions, effective dates, rates, or taxability treatment.
requiredReviewToReclassify: Current official local ordinance or code section
Current official rate schedule or agreement
Assessor, treasurer, or tax agency confirmation

unsupportedTriageRules.sourcePattern: Opportunity terms include rebate, grant, loan, financing, PACE, REC, SREC, tariff, net metering, interconnection, procurement preference, certification, permit, or technical assistance, and the official source does not reduce a tax liability, tax base, assessed value, tax rate, or filing amount.
unsupportedTriageRules.repairQueueReason: Do not repair inside the tax engine unless an official source separately identifies a tax credit, deduction, exemption, rate preference, special valuation, abatement, or tax-line reduction.
codexActions: Set taxValueEligible to false.
Route to rebate_financing_or_program_ops if RetroFi has a non-tax incentive module.
Do not label the amount as tax savings.
Do not infer taxability from program marketing language.
sourceBackedFacts: A tax credit or deduction changes a tax bill or taxable income; a financing product repaid through a property assessment is not itself a tax saving.
examples: C-PACE financing marketed as tax-bill repayment
Utility rebate for heat pumps
State grant for solar storage
Net-metering tariff

unsupportedTriageRules.sourcePattern: Opportunity appears tax-related but the importer has no official source, only a secondary summary, a broken source URL, a paywalled source, a stale screenshot, or a source that does not identify the tax authority.
unsupportedTriageRules.repairQueueReason: Official source discovery is required before model mapping, effective-date validation, or customer-facing savings.
codexActions: Keep the opportunity record for discovery.
Do not populate rates, formulas, caps, or local adoptions from secondary summaries.
Queue source discovery with jurisdiction, tax type, and program name.
Suppress from customer-facing tax totals.
sourceBackedFacts: The controlling import policy requires official tax, statutory, regulatory, assessor, treasurer, municipal, form-instruction, or official GIS/data sources wherever possible and prohibits invented rates, formulas, local adoptions, effective dates, or taxability treatment.
examples: DSIRE-only tax summary with no live agency or statute link
Vendor blog says sales tax exemption exists but no tax agency citation
Archived PDF says program existed but no current statute or filing form is available

unsupportedTriageRules.sourcePattern: Official source says the tax provision expired, sunsets before the relevant tax period, was repealed, was revoked, is closed to new applicants, or applies only to awards already made and the opportunity lacks a transition rule covering the taxpayer.
unsupportedTriageRules.repairQueueReason: Archive or suppress unless an official extension, transition provision, or taxpayer-specific grandfathering document is found.
codexActions: Store the official end date.
Compare the end date to project placed-in-service date, purchase date, application date, and tax period.
If taxpayer-specific grandfathering is possible, change to human_review_required rather than calculated.
Do not estimate savings after the official end date.
sourceBackedFacts: Official statutes may contain specific expiration dates that control whether a tax preference can be claimed for a tax period.
examples: Solar manufacturing B&O preference after statutory sunset with no extension
Expired sales tax holiday
Closed tax-credit allocation round
Repealed local property tax exemption

unsupportedTriageRules.sourcePattern: Official source identifies a sales or use tax rate, exemption, refund, deduction, resale rule, or taxability treatment for equipment or services, and official rate or boundary data can resolve the applicable jurisdiction from the delivery or use location.
unsupportedTriageRules.repairQueueReason: Repair into sales_use_tax_rate or sales_use_tax_exemption only when official taxability, combined rate, address-level jurisdiction, taxable basis, and filing or certificate requirements are available.
codexActions: Require install, delivery, or use address before calculating rate.
Require taxable purchase amount and invoice classification.
Require official taxability source for equipment, labor, software, services, freight, or installation charges.
For exemptions, require exemption certificate, reseller permit, refund claim, or filing confirmation when the source requires one.
Default customerFacingValueCents to 0 until all runtime gates are satisfied.
sourceBackedFacts: Washington DOR says sales tax has state and local portions, local rates vary by city or county, and retailers collect based on where the customer receives goods or services.
Washington DOR provides an address or map-based sales and use tax rate lookup and says rate data are updated quarterly.
examples: Manufacturing machinery and equipment sales tax exemption
